title: Molecular basis for DNA cleavage by the mini-RNA-guided endonuclease Casδ−1
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: CRISPR-Cas adaptive immune systems are powerful and versatile tools for genome engineering. CRISPR-Casδ−1 is a recently discovered, evolutionarily distinct endonuclease that enables versatile cross-kingdom genome editing under miniature RNA-guiding. In this study, we present a comprehensive biochemical and structural characterization of CRISPR-Casδ−1. Biochemical analysis not only verifies that Casδ−1 exhibits robust double-stranded DNA cleavage activity and target-dependent trans-cleavage activity, but also explores in depth its precise cleavage sites and substrate saturation. Furthermore, we determine a 3.04 Å resolution cryo-EM structure of the Casδ−1-crRNA-dsDNA ternary complex, which reveals the molecular basis of protospacer-adjacent motif (PAM) recognition, crRNA-DNA heteroduplex assembly, and RuvC domain-mediated DNA cleavage. Collectively, our study reveals the structural basis and evolutionary insights into Casδ−1, advances the mechanistic understanding of type V CRISPR-Cas effectors, and offers opportunities for the rational design of CRISPR-Casδ−1 as a versatile genome-editing tool.

title: Evaluating anonymized genome re-identification using polygenic predictions and its implications for data privacy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Re-identification by phenotypic prediction aims to determine whether a genome belongs to a specific individual by comparing the individual’s known traits with those predicted from the genome. Although this tracing attack is widely discussed in the genomic privacy literature, its practical risk remains uncertain. As genome-wide association studies (GWAS) continue to improve phenotypic prediction, concerns about the potential for this attack increase.Here, to quantify its real-world threat, we develop a probabilistic framework that estimates the likelihood of a match between an individual’s observed traits and polygenic scores (PGS) derived from a genome, while accounting for prediction accuracy and genetic and environmental correlations between traits. We benchmark this re-identification method and examine how the prior probability that a random genome and set of traits correspond to the same person affects performance. Finally, we assess whether sensitive genetic information, such as APOE-ε4 status (linked with Alzheimer’s disease) can be inferred through this attack. Our method outperforms a state-of-the-art tool, reaching a precision above 99% for a recall of 40% when considering a prior of 50%. However, in real-world settings, we estimate that realistic priors do not exceed 4 × 10−4%, resulting in a precision lower than 0.13% at the same recall. Inference of sensitive genetic variants also proves ineffective: precision above 50% for identifying APOE-ε4 carriers is achieved only at a recall below 20%. Thus, although re-identification by phenotypic prediction is technically feasible, its effectiveness in real-world conditions remains limited.

title: Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Noninvasive multitarget delivery of size-diverse therapeutics, including extracellular vesicles (EVs) and mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), to peri-infarct zones is hindered by the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and heterogeneous infarct topographies. Here, we developed a hologram-assisted multitarget BBB opening (HaMBO) platform combining low-cost 3D-printed holograms with a single-element ultrasound transducer. Spatially tailored acoustic fields enabled localized BBB opening along infarct borders. In male mice with transient focal cerebral ischemia, a single two-minute HaMBO treatment safely enhanced the peri-infarct delivery of EVs and MSCs, reduced brain atrophy by ~56%, increased angiogenesis by ~2-fold and neural progenitor proliferation by ~4-fold, and improved long-term behavioral recovery. Spatial transcriptomic analysis associated HaMBO-assisted EV therapy with reduced macrophage infiltration and enhanced pro-angiogenic and neurogenic signaling. Human skull-based simulations further demonstrated HaMBO’s clinical adaptability across diverse stroke scenarios. Thus, HaMBO provides a safe, low-cost, and customizable platform for noninvasive multitarget delivery in ischemic stroke and other neurological disorders.

title: Structural dynamics of substrate processing by the p97-Ufd1-Npl4-FAF1 machinery
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The AAA-ATPase VCP/p97 unfolds ubiquitylated proteins in key signaling and cellular homeostasis pathways, yet the mechanisms by which Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 adapters handle ubiquitin chains to coordinate substrate loading and processing remain unclear. Our cryo-EM study of p97-Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 engaging a substrate reveal interactions that drive substrate processing. While Npl4 is capped by distal ubiquitins, and the initiator ubiquitin can be traced from the Npl4 groove to the ATPase channel at near-atomic resolution, we find that the Npl4 tower adaptively responds to the configurational changes in the ATPase motor’s spiral staircase. A helix in FAF1 together with the Ufd1-UT3 domain engage proximal ubiquitins while providing the necessary structural plasticity to accommodate this motion and deliver ubiquitins to Npl4’s groove. Our study reveals the intricate, dynamic interplay between p97, Ufd1-Npl4, and FAF1 in efficient processing of ubiquitylated substrates.

title: Spatiotemporal proteomics reveals dynamic antiparallel gradients shaping signalling waves
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Embryonic development is driven by dynamic protein networks, yet how these dynamics shape morphogenesis remains poorly understood. Somitogenesis, the rhythmic segmentation of vertebrate embryos, is controlled by signalling gradients and oscillations in the presomitic mesoderm (PSM), but the underlying protein dynamics remain largely unknown. Here, we combine microfluidic synchronisation of mouse embryo tails with quantitative proteomics and transcriptomics to resolve spatiotemporal protein dynamics during somitogenesis. We identify proteins with dynamic expression during somitogenesis and reveal an antiparallel, dynamic R-Spondin/LGR signalling pattern that explains how Wnt oscillation amplitude increases despite declining Wnt ligand levels in the anterior PSM. Dynamic ligand expression is validated in mouse gastruloids, and perturbation of ligand dynamics reduces oscillation amplitude and impairs somite formation. Together, our findings identify R-Spondin as a dynamic amplifier of Wnt signalling oscillations and provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how protein dynamics regulate mammalian tissue patterning.

title: NYNRIN safeguards leukemia stem cells by sustaining thioredoxin activity to maintain redox homeostasis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Leukemia stem cells (LSCs) primarily rely on mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) for energy production, a metabolic feature that inevitably generates excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS). NYNRIN (NYN domain and retroviral integrase containing) is highly expressed in LSC-like cells and is associated with poor prognosis in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Genetic targeting of NYNRIN impairs LSC-like cell maintenance and in vivo leukemogenic capacity in MLL-AF9- and HOXA9/MEIS1-driven AML models, and compromises the in vivo pathogenicity of patient-derived LSC-like cells. Mechanistically, NYNRIN sustains thioredoxin (Trx) activity by functioning as an RNA-binding protein that directly binds and degrades TXNIP mRNA via its NYN domain. Loss of NYNRIN stabilizes TXNIP mRNA, leading to TXNIP accumulation, which disrupts Trx-mediated redox buffering, induces ROS overproduction and mitochondrial dysfunction, and triggers LSC apoptosis. Notably, NYNRIN inhibition potentiates venetoclax efficacy by compromising Trx-mediated ROS clearance, lowering the apoptotic threshold of LSCs. Collectively, our findings reveal a critical NYNRIN-TXNIP-Trx axis that safeguards LSCs by enabling efficient ROS clearance.

title: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Dense Associative Memories (DenseAMs) are generalizations of Hopfield networks that store training data at local minima of the energy landscape. When the amount of training data exceeds the critical memory storage capacity, new local minima (different from the training data) emerge. These emergent local minima, known as spurious states, can hinder memory retrieval. We examine diffusion models (DMs) through the DenseAM lens, viewing their generative process as an attempt of a memory retrieval. In the small data regime, DMs create distinct attractors for each training sample, akin to DenseAMs below the critical capacity. As the training set size increases, DMs transition to generalization. We identify a critical intermediate phase, predicted by DenseAM theory, characterized by the emergence of spurious states. In generative modeling, these previously overlooked states are no longer negative artifacts but rather are the first signs of generative capabilities. Their existence is demonstrated across a wide range of architectures and datasets.

title: Bridging Spectroscopy and Reactivity: Identifying the True Reactive CO Species in Electrocatalytic CO Oxidation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In situ electrochemical vibrational spectroscopy has revolutionized our understanding of electrocatalysis. However, establishing a rigorous correlation between spectroscopic signatures and reaction kinetics is still very challenging because high-coverage surface species may dominate the signal, whereas the truly reactive participants may be short-lived or spectroscopically silent. To disentangle spectators from true reaction participants, we developed a high-sensitivity spectroelectrochemical platform that integrates the rotating disk electrode with surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (RDE-SERS). This approach enables the simultaneous acquisition of reaction kinetics and interfacial molecular information under well-defined mass transport conditions. Using this versatile approach, we investigated the benchmark carbon monoxide oxidation reaction (COOR) on the Pt surface, which enabled decoupling between the spectroscopically observable species and the catalytically active species. Despite persistent and intense Raman signatures of adsorbed CO (COad) in the diffusion-limited region, COad predominantly acts as a spectator that blocks surface sites without effectively participating in the reaction, as confirmed by the isotope substitution experiments. Conversely, the oxidation current is sustained by the continuous flux of solution-phase CO (COsol), which is identified as the kinetically relevant reactant. These findings offer a new perspective on the roles of adsorbed species versus solution-phase species during dynamic electrochemical reactions. Collectively, the RDE-SERS methodology is established as a reliable strategy for identifying true reaction pathways, bridging molecular-level spectroscopic identification with macroscopic reactivity in complex electrocatalytic systems.

title: Toward net-zero building: an optimisation methodology for passive and active retrofits with renewable integration – a UK office building case study
abstract: Existing commercial buildings account for a large share of energy use and carbon emissions, highlighting the need for net-zero retrofit strategies. This study develops an integrated framework for building retrofits, combining calibrated building energy simulation with multi-source renewable energy system design and optimisation to reduce energy demand, maximise on-site renewable generation, and enable cost-effective decarbonisation. A calibrated energy model was created in DesignBuilder to evaluate retrofit measures, while renewable energy systems and storage were optimised for maximum renewable fractions using HOMER Pro. A two-stage MATLAB-based Pareto front and TOPSIS multi-criteria optimisation evaluated and ranked retrofit configurations. The framework was applied to a UK office building case study (hot-summer, cold-winter climate), identifying the optimal configuration, which combines lighting upgrades, office equipment improvements, a water-to-water ground-source heat pump, carport-mounted solar PV, and rooftop horizontal-axis wind turbines. The retrofit reduces annual energy demand by 38.4% and achieves an average renewable fraction of 66.3%, reducing net grid energy import by 91.53%, with on-site generation exceeding demand during peak summer months. Annual CO 2 emissions decrease by 39.0% after retrofitting and by 86.1% after the integration of renewables compared to the baseline model of the case-study building. Economic analysis shows strong financial viability, with a levelized cost of £0.172/kWh and a payback period of 6.48 years. Sensitivity analyses confirm the solution remains optimal under varying energy prices and stakeholder priorities, demonstrating robustness for commercial deployment. The results highlight the framework's ability to guide transferable, multi-criteria retrofit planning and support deep operational decarbonisation across diverse building types.

title: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Head direction (HD) cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus form the brain’s internal compass, and are often modeled as a ring attractor maintaining azimuth coding by leveraging continuous visual and inertial sensory input. Here, we test how the common experimental preparation of head-fixed animals alters this code. Complete head-fixation that creates vestibular conflict disrupts both unit and population encoding of head direction, while selectively constraining head-on-body movements either in real or virtual reality uniquely impairs HD population activity. More specifically, attractor dynamics are altered in head-restrained male mice during periods of immobility, and a computational model recapitulates this effect by perturbing lateral connectivity among HD neurons. These dynamics recover several hundred milliseconds prior to locomotion onset, suggesting that an efference copy or prediction of a re-afferent signal is necessary to maintain HD network activity during head restraint. More generally, the results indicate that the HD network is a context- and state-dependent predictive estimator, stabilized by forthcoming self-motion signals. The classic ring-attractor models should be revised to integrate context-dependent dynamics with prospective motor signals, offering a more complete account of how the brain’s compass remains stable across both naturalistic and constrained conditions.

title: Structure and function of cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal Toc159/Toc90 as a chloroplast protein import pore
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chloroplast protein-import channel Toc75 evolved from a cyanobacterial outer-membrane Omp85 protein, despite all known Omp85 proteins functioning in export. Chlamydomonas Toc75 assembles with Toc90M, the membrane-spanning domain of Toc90 (equivalent of higher-plant Toc159) into a binocular-shaped complex, but how this architecture arose and functions in import remain unknown. Here, cryo-electron microscopy and mutational analysis of a cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal a lidded 16-β-strand barrel and three POTRA-domains involved in assembling outer-membrane proteins. Structural comparisons show that the Toc75–Toc90M complex mirrors an Omp85–substrate assembly intermediate, and Toc90M can indeed serve as a bacterial Omp85 substrate. While canonical Omp85 systems release substrates after assembly, Toc75 evolved a basic patch in its barrel to anchor Toc90M as a stable lateral pore through which precursor proteins are imported. Our findings indicate that a bacterial export system was converted into a chloroplast import channel by locking a substrate in place to provide an import conduit. This requirement for a stable assembly also supports that additional parts of the ancestral complex, including Omp85 POTRA-domains and Tic236 orthologs, were recruited to facilitate chloroplast protein import.

title: Geopolitical energy shocks and consumer protection under fiscal constraints
abstract: How can energy-importing governments protect fuel-dependent households during geopolitical crises without suppressing conservation incentives or making unaffordable fiscal promises? We develop conditional insurance based on pre-crisis reference fuel consumption, with transfers independent of current purchases. Under stated assumptions, fixed payments preserve the marginal pump-price signal; a strictly concave allocation problem determines how to distribute scarce assistance. A dated liquidity rule prioritizes binding infrastructure guarantees and committed low-carbon investment before discretionary relief, and identifies the conditions under which protection must be rationed or financing fails. Guarantees require verified project-specific external losses and contractual caps. French monthly fuel-price analyses for 2020–2026, a longer exploratory global VAR, and a European synthetic-control comparison of France’s September 2022 intervention illustrate implementation. The latter captures a combined public–private discount and has low-powered donor placebos; it does not isolate the causal effect of the state rebate. Externally released geopolitical energy and macro surprises provide additional exploratory transmission diagnostics; their underlying structural model is not re-estimated and French event samples remain sparse. The framework offers conditional, auditable policy rules rather than a demonstrated universal welfare ranking or unconditional sovereign solvency.

title: Dual-point-groups engineering enable multi-ultrahigh-Q resonances via Brillouin zone folding in tetramer metasurfaces
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-Q resonances based on bound states in the continuum provide a central route of enhancing light-matter interactions. Here, we present a dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding. By selectively preserving or reducing the O- and S-group symmetries of super lattice, guided modes below light cone can be converted into guided resonances or bound states in the continuum with controlled degeneracy lifting, Q-factor scaling, eigenfield profiles, and mode splitting. Besides, applying rectangular lattice provides an alternative way of tuning the Q-factors and mode splitting. Finally, we experimentally demonstrate such two types of high-Q resonances in the tetramer metasurfaces. Measurement results show that the mode splitting can be tuned from 0 nm to 70 nm while the Q-factors are modulated from 300 to 20,000 by varying the asymmetry parameters. This work establishes a symmetry-addressed route for programmable multi-resonant high-Q metasurfaces.

title: Programmable roll-to-roll laser processing for high value application of low-grade carbon fiber materials
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Growing production of carbon fibers generates substantial short-chopped fibers that are difficult for high-value use due to their structural discontinuity. Carbon fiber felts offer potential, yet weak inter-fiber bonding and poor conductivity limit the performance. We report a roll‑to‑roll laser processing strategy that uses a liquid precursor to form laser‑induced graphene at fiber‑fiber interfaces, creating conductive pathways and mechanical interconnections. This approach increases tensile strength from 4.1 to 32.2 MPa and electrical conductivity from 1224.0 to 15151.5 S/m. The resulting films demonstrate efficient electrothermal de‑icing and, after copper deposition, lightning strike protection with a damage area of 9657 mm² and depth of 0.4 mm, comparable to aluminum mesh but with 15% lower weight. A custom‑built laser platform enables scalable production. Here, we show the conversion of low‑grade carbon fibers into lightweight, functional films for aerospace applications via scalable laser processing.

title: From microstructure to function: spatial visualization of magnetic permeability
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding the physics of high-frequency magnetic response is essential for advancing electromagnetic materials. Here, a general strategy is presented for visualizing magnetic permeability as a spatially distributed, frequency-dependent field, instead of a uniform bulk parameter. Our framework reveals that high-frequency magnetic loss arises from coherent spin-wave propagation and interference, leading to spatially selective energy absorption and localized regions of negative imaginary permeability. Tailoring geometric connectivity to suppress spin-wave propagation enables the selective enhancement of localized resonances. Such resonance enables deterministic control over high-frequency response through structural design. The principle is further examined in nanoscale iron spheres. Their surface morphology plays a decisive role in reorganizing the internal resonance domains. This structural reconfiguration, in turn, reshapes the broadband magnetic permeability spectra. To navigate the high-dimensional space of surface defect configurations, machine learning models are integrated with micromagnetic simulations, allowing rapid prediction of magnetic performance across microwave bands. Computational modeling provides an ideal platform to complement experimental exploration. The physic-data framework reveals geometry-to-spectra design rules, validated on iron nanoparticles. This framework uniquely bridges the microscopic spin dynamics with electromagnetic response, enabling tunable high-frequency materials for communication and sensing.

title: Superior energy-storage performance in BaTiO3-based MLCCs via high-entropy driven multiscale optimization
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Multilayer ceramic capacitors are essential components in modern electronic devices. However, achieving superior performance under high-temperature and high-electric-field remains a huge challenge due to the increased leakage current and limited breakdown strength. Herein, a high-entropy driven multiscale optimization strategy is proposed for lead-free multilayer ceramic capacitors. This approach integrates multiple elements into both A- and B-sites at the atomic scale, engineers polymorphic domain coexistence at the phase scale, and introduces a uniform SiO2 coating layer on grain surfaces to form a core–shell structure while refining grain size at the grain scale. Furthermore, a SiO2 barrier layer is constructed between the electrodes and ceramics at the device scale. Remarkably, high-entropy BaTiO3-based Multilayer ceramic capacitors achieve an ultra-high energy density of 19.8 J·cm−3 and a high efficiency of 89.3% at 1421 kV·cm−1, along with an outstanding high-temperature energy storage performance. The high-entropy driven multiscale optimization strategy offers a universal approach to enhancing the overall energy storage performance of advanced dielectric capacitors.

title: A multi-functionally integrated modular catalyst for efficient chemoselective hydrogenation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chemoselective hydrogenation of nitroarenes containing multiple reducible groups remains challenging due to the intrinsic activity–selectivity trade-off of conventional metal catalysts. Here we report a multi-functional Pt-based catalyst, modularly integrating molecular-sieving feedstock separation, hydrogen activation, intermediate transport and surface reaction like a nanofactory. Structurally, ~3 nm Pt nanoparticles supported on sodium titanate are encapsulated by oxygen vacancies-enriched TiOx overlayers that only permit hydrogen to adsorb on Pt particles for dissociation while preventing substrate contact. The generated active hydrogen species subsequently migrate to the catalyst surface and hydrogenate nitro groups adsorbed on surface Lewis basic oxygen vacancies, enabling an efficient condensation pathway while avoiding the use of corrosive and environmentally unfriendly alkaline solvents. The spatially decoupled yet functionally synergistic catalytic design achieves 90% 3-vinylaniline yield from 3-nitrostyrene under mild conditions with an unprecedented turnover frequency of 83,200 h−1, exceeding all previously reported metal catalysts, and exhibits broad generality toward diverse substituted nitroarenes. Collectively, these findings provide a powerful catalyst design strategy for steering complex reaction networks via spatially modular catalysis.

title: Arabian hydroclimate and hominin population dynamics over the last 500,000 years
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite the discovery of a rich Palaeolithic archaeological record in Arabia over the last decade, the environmental context of hominin occupations and dispersals remains poorly understood owing to the paucity of Pleistocene palaeoenvironmental records. Here we show a multi-proxy, high-resolution dust record from the western equatorial Indian Ocean spanning the last 500,000 years, which enables evaluation of the influence of orbital-scale hydrological variations on hominin populations in Arabia. The dust evidence reinforces the view that hominin presence in Arabia was driven by enhanced monsoon precipitation during so-called Green Arabia periods. These results, coupled with hunter-gatherer demographic data, point to marked hominin population expansions during prolonged wetter periods. Hominin occupation, however, was not linked exclusively to traditional humid periods. Brief phases of high-intensity rainfall within some glacial periods, manifested by transient high dust contents associated with enhanced terrestrial moisture availability and increased supply of wind-erodible particles, also favoured hominin expansions.

title: Complementary axes of functional system integrity and integration with divergent clinical correlates characterize focal epilepsy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Focal epilepsy affects distributed brain systems, yet characterizations of patient-specific network organization that are clinically meaningful remain limited. Using resting-state functional MRI, we estimated overlapping individualized networks and derived two complementary axes (1) network correspondence, indexing system integrity through canonical system expression, and (2) k-hubness, indexing cross-system integration through multi-network participation. We studied a presurgical cohort of 305 patients with focal epilepsy and 224 healthy participants and an independent validation cohort of 903 patients spanning focal and common generalized and childhood epilepsy syndromes and 666 healthy participants. Correspondence disruption was broadly shared across focal epilepsies, whereas k-hubness alterations showed lateralized and syndrome-dependent redistributions of cross-system integration. The axes shared variance but showed modest preferential associations, with correspondence relating to cognition and k-hubness to epilepsy clinical features. Together, these measures characterize common and heterogeneous alterations in individualized brain system organization, linking complementary aspects of network topology to cognitive and clinical variation.

title: Making 1000 Wh/kg LiNiO2 Cathode Nearly Strain-Free by Complex-Concentrated Doping
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract High-energy batteries require cathodes with greater capacity and specific energy. Ni-rich-layered oxides approach the performance limit of LiNiO2 (LNO), yet its practical use is hindered by severe chemomechanical degradation. Near 4.2 V, the H2-H3/H4 transition drives substantial c-axis contraction, volume shrinkage, O1 formation, oxygen loss, and rapid capacity decay. Here, we show that only 5% cobalt-free complex concentrated doping stabilizes LNO without sacrificing energy density. The modified LNO reduces c-axis strain from 7.4 to 2.1%, exhibits near-zero-strain behavior, and delivers 258 mAh•g–1 and 973 Wh•kg–1. In pouch cells, it retains 80% capacity after 1800 cycles and shows markedly improved thermal stability. These results demonstrate that complex-concentrated doping at low dopant loading can suppress strain and phase transformations at the full-Ni limit, providing a broadly applicable strategy for stabilizing high-energy intercalation electrodes while preserving their intrinsic capacity and specific energy during prolonged electrochemical cycling.

title: Dual Functions of Halogen-Bonding Molecules for Stabilizing Ultra-wide Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) metal halide perovskite solar cells are essential for multi-junction solar cells with higher power conversion efficiency (PCE) potentials. In this work, we report the dual functions of 5-iodoisophthalic acid (I-BDC) to suppress phase segregation and uncoordinated Pb2+ related defects to enhance UWBG perovskite cell performance and stability. An I-BDC incorporated 1.95 eV perovskite film exhibited stable photoluminescence after 120 min of illumination. The best I-BDC cell achieved a certified reverse scan PCE of 16.5%, the highest for 1.95 eV perovskite cells to date. These UWBG perovskite solar cells are the most stable reported to date, with one encapsulated device retaining 90% of its initial PCE after 500 h of maximum power point tracking at ∼40 °C and another retaining 95% of its initial PCE after 206 thermal cycles (–40 ↔ 85 °C), passing the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 61215 testing protocols at the cell level.

title: rGO-MXene 2D Interfacial Engineering for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability of Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In this work, we report an innovative interface engineering strategy combining bidirectional chemical anchoring and electronic bridging via a 2D reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and MXene conductive network. This hierarchical 2D structure suppresses the aggregation and stacking of single-layer MXene nanosheets while mutually compensating for individual charge transport limitations. Specifically, the abundant functional groups passivate interfacial defects (Pb2+ and I–) and bond with the PCBM layer via coordination, hydrogen bonding and π–π interactions. This synergistic architecture lowers the electron energy offset. Consequently, PSCs incorporating the rGO-MXene interlayer achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.96% (certified 25.05%) and retain 96.43% of initial efficiency after 1000 h in ambient air. Furthermore, 10 × 10 cm2 large-area PSM yields a high PCE of 20.25%, maintaining 96.05% of initial efficiency under maximum power point tracking for 963 h.

title: Alicyclic Lewis Bases Enable 100 °C-Processed α-FAPbI3 Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Formamidinium lead iodide (α-FAPbI3) perovskite, despite its ideal bandgap, requires high-temperature (≥150 °C) annealing for the δ-to-α phase transformation, hindering its application in low-temperature processed inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), particularly on flexible substrates. Herein, we demonstrate that the alicyclic Lewis base caprolactam (CPL) effectively drives the complete δ-to-α phase transformation of FAPbI3 at a reduced temperature of 100 °C. Experiments and theoretical calculations reveal that CPL lowers the phase transition energy barrier and retards crystallization kinetics via strong Pb2+ coordination and controlled desorption. This strategy yields highly crystalline, fully phase-converted α-FAPbI3 films with improved morphology, reduced defect densities, and enhanced optoelectronic properties. Consequently, CPL-modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.64% with good operational stability. The low-temperature processability also enables high-performance flexible PSCs with a PCE of 23.73%. This work presents an additive engineering approach for realizing efficient and stable α-FAPbI3 PSCs through low-temperature manufacturing.

title: Structured Filler-Enabled Pore-Interface Engineering in Polydimethylsiloxane for Passive Radiative Cooling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Passive radiative cooling (PRC) materials require efficient solar scattering, high thermal emissivity, and mechanical compliance, yet constructing hierarchical pore-interface architectures that simultaneously enhance particle scattering, interface scattering, and flexibility within a single polymer system remains challenging. Here, we report a structured filler-induced pore-interface engineering strategy for flexible PRC films. Carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) and silane-modified SiO2 nanoparticles were electrostatically assembled into a spatially organized CMC@SiO2 filler, which simultaneously acts as a scattering unit and a pore-forming scaffold. Upon incorporation into polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), the structured filler induces hierarchical pore architectures with SiO2-decorated pore walls, generating coupled particle-scattering and pore-interface scattering pathways. The Finite-Difference Time-Domain simulations reveal that the multiscale architecture broadens solar scattering across the 0.25–2.5 μm range through enhanced refractive-index contrast and multiple-scattering effects. Benefiting from the coupled contribution of SiO2 scattering centers, hierarchical pore interfaces, and the intrinsic mid-infrared (MIR) emissivity of PDMS, the resulting film achieves a solar reflectivity of 94.6% and a MIR emissivity of 95.2%. The film delivers a maximum sub-ambient cooling of 7.1 °C under direct sunlight. Building energy simulations further predict an average annual cooling-energy reduction of 10.4% across representative climate zones in China. This work establishes a structured filler-enabled hierarchical pore-interface engineering strategy that integrates scattering enhancement, porous architectures, and polymer flexibility, offering a general route toward scalable and high-performance PRC materials.

title: Sustainable Thermoplastic Thermal Interface Adhesive Derived from Poly(lipoic acid) and Boron Nitride for Efficient Electronic Thermal Management
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The escalating power density of electronics demands thermal interface materials (TIMs) that simultaneously offer high thermal conductivity, strong adhesion, and environmental sustainability. Conventional thermally conductive adhesives (TCAs) face inherent trade-offs among these properties, often relying on non-recyclable thermosets. Here, we present a sustainable thermoplastic TCA composed of a poly(lipoic acid) (polyLA)-based dynamic polymer matrix integrated with polyvinylpyrrolidone-modified hexagonal boron nitride (BN@PVP). The polyLA matrix incorporates catechol moieties and reversible Fe3+-carboxyl/catechol coordination bonds, creating a dynamically reconfigurable network. This design yields an adhesive (LD50Fe100) with high toughness (1.52 MJ m–3), and strong lap shear adhesion (884 kPa on PMMA and 1210 kPa on steel). The dynamic bonds enable room-temperature self-healing (93.1% efficiency) and robust recyclability. At a BN@PVP loading of 40 wt %, the composite (BN@LD50Fe100) achieves a thermal conductivity of 1.2 W m–1 K–1 while maintaining enhanced mechanical properties. LED chip heat dissipation experiments demonstrate a 4 °C lower operating temperature compared to devices without a TIM, with stable thermal performance over multiple cycles. This work provides a promising material strategy to overcome the traditional trade-offs in TCAs, offering a path toward repairable, reusable, and efficient thermal management solutions for advanced electronic packaging.

title: Bamboo-Inspired Homogeneous Porous Aerogel via Gas Foaming Assisted by Freeze-Drying for High-Sensitivity Flexible Pressure Sensors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Flexible piezoresistive sensors are pivotal in personalized healthcare. However, simultaneously achieving high sensitivity and a broad linear range remains a formidable challenge owing to rapid structural densification of porous materials. Inspired by the multiscale composite structure of bamboo, this study addresses the existing challenge by proposing a novel MXene aerogel sensor, reinforced by compounding cellulose nanofiber (CNF) Several instances of CNFs (which were introduced during copyediting) have been reverted back to CNF, consistent with our original submission where the abbreviation was defined as cellulose nanofiber (CNF). Corresponding grammatical adjustments are made to match this usage. This change only standardizes the abbreviation and does not alter any scientific content. and bamboo cellulose. By leveraging a uniform conductive network constructed on CNF (simulating bamboo parenchyma cells to disperse the vascular bundles) and the supporting effect of the bamboo cellulose skeleton (mimicking vascular bundles to provide support), premature collapse is effectively resisted. Moreover, inspired by the hollow cell cavity structure of bamboo, a stable porous architecture is constructed via gas foaming and freeze-drying, enabling it to effectively reconcile the inherent trade-off between sensitivity and the detection range. The sensor exhibits a high sensitivity of 148.29 kPa–1 (0–15 kPa) and a wide effective working range extending up to 100 kPa. This superior electromechanical performance enables the precise detection of full-spectrum physiological signals ranging from subtle pulse waveforms to large-scale joint movements and facilitates assistive rehabilitation for post-stroke finger therapy via human–computer interaction. Augmented by a support vector machine algorithm, the sensor has a wireless sleep monitoring capability and achieves a high classification accuracy of 96.5% in identifying distinct breathing states. The proposed sensor demonstrates significant application potential in next-generation intelligent home health management systems.

title: Interfacial Kinetic Matching in Amorphous Fe2O3/Crystalline Cu2O Enables Efficient Nitrate-To-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical nitrate (NO3–) reduction to ammonia (NH3) is a promising route for simultaneous nitrate remediation and sustainable NH3 synthesis, yet remains challenged by sluggish multistep hydrogenation kinetics. Here, we report an amorphous Fe2O3/crystalline Cu2O catalyst (a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O), in which ultrasmall Cu2O nanocrystallites are uniformly dispersed in an amorphous Fe2O3 matrix. The resulting a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O interface induces strong electronic interaction and complementary catalytic functions. The pH-dependent potential analysis shows that a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O maintains a highly alkaline interfacial microenvironment, while stepwise kinetic measurements reveal favorable kinetic matching between NO3– activation and subsequent NO2– hydrogenation. In situ spectroscopic studies reveal a tandem catalytic pathway in which NO3– is first activated on c-Cu2O to form NO2–, followed by transfer to adjacent a-Fe2O3 sites for hydrogenation to NH3. Consequently, a-Fe2O3/c-Cu2O achieves an NH3 Faradaic efficiency of 92.4% and an NH3 yield rate of 6.25 mmol h–1 mg–1, and sustains stable operation for 100 h in a membrane electrode assembly electrolyzer. This work offers a viable strategy for promoting nitrate-to-ammonia electrosynthesis through amorphous/crystalline interfacial engineering.

title: Synergistic Coordination Regulation and Nanofiller-Guided Ion Transport in a Polyacrylamide Gel Electrolyte for Highly Reversible Aqueous Zn Metal Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Despite their safety and cost advantages, aqueous zinc-ion batteries remain limited by the instability of Zn metal anodes, including nonuniform deposition, dendrite growth, and parasitic reactions. A PAM/CMC-Na/CNTs (PCC) hydrogel electrolyte is constructed by incorporating sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC-Na) and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) into a polyacrylamide (PAM) matrix. The –COO– and –OH groups of CMC-Na regulate the local coordination environment of Zn2+ and suppress water-related side reactions, while CNTs reinforce the gel network and improve interfacial contact. PCC exhibits an ionic conductivity of 24.16 mS cm–1 and an apparent Zn2+ transference number of 0.791. These transport characteristics, together with interfacial analyses, are consistent with more uniform Zn deposition. Zn//Zn symmetric cells cycle stably for over 2300 h at 1 mA cm–2 with an areal capacity of 1 mAh cm–2 and for approximately 550 h at 5 mA cm–2 with a capacity of 5 mAh cm–2. Zn//Cu cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.94%, while Zn//MnO2 full cells retain 81.64% capacity after 700 cycles at 1 A g–1. A high-loading Zn//MnO2 pouch cell further demonstrates favorable energy-storage performance. This work presents a strategy for designing hydrogel electrolytes that integrate coordination regulation, homogenized ion transport, and mechanical robustness.

title: Hierarchical Functionalized Lignin Interfaces Regulate Water Transport in Low-Coating-Content Bio-Based Polyurethane-Coated Urea
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bio-based polyurethane coatings are promising for controlled-release fertilizers, but their release performance at low coating contents is often limited by rapid surface wetting and water transport through the coating membrane. Here, we constructed a hierarchical lignin-based interface on castor-oil-derived polyurethane-coated urea to regulate water–coating interactions. Lignin micro/nanospheres were sequentially functionalized with polydopamine and octadecyltrichlorosilane and introduced at the outer polyurethane interface during the final coating stage. Thermodynamic calculations and spectroscopic analyses were consistent with interfacial chemical coupling between polydopamine-associated functional groups and residual isocyanate groups in the polyurethane coating. The resulting interface increased the apparent water contact angle from 87.4° to 157.2°, weakened the calculated adsorption of water, and reduced water-vapor permeability through the coating. Under a nominal total coating-material input of approximately 3 wt %, the cumulative nitrogen release within 10 days decreased from 56% for bio-based polyurethane-coated urea (BCU) to 20% for OTS-LMNPs@PDA-modified bio-based controlled-release urea (SBCU), while the time required to reach 80% nitrogen release increased from 20 to 49 days. This enhanced release performance was associated with reduced surface wetting, lower water affinity, and slower water transport across the modified coating, which collectively delayed water penetration, urea dissolution, and subsequent nitrogen diffusion. These results demonstrate that lignin-based interfacial modification provides an effective strategy for regulating water transport and improving the controlled-release performance of low-coating-content bio-based polyurethane fertilizers.

title: An Organic–Inorganic Hybrid Memristor with Trap-Assisted Hopping for Synaptic Plasticity and Artificial Nociceptor
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Neuromorphic hardware demands artificial synaptic devices that mimic biological synapses. Achieving multifunctional emulation of synaptic plasticity and nociceptive behavior in a single, highly stable, low-power device remains a major challenge. In this report, zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnONP) are synthesized via a surfactant-assisted sol–gel method. These are incorporated into an organic small-molecule matrix of 6,13-bis(triisopropylsilylethynyl)pentacene (TP) to fabricate a solution-processed organic–inorganic hybrid memristor. The as-fabricated hybrid memristor mimicked artificial synaptic behavior at a low operating voltage (<±1 V) while demonstrating high stability with retention exceeding 105 s in ambient atmosphere. The TP/ZnONP-based memristor has illustrated both short-term and long-term synaptic plasticity, facilitating the exemplification of learning and memory functions of biological synapses. The memristor has been found to exhibit pain-perception-related nociceptive behavior, including protective responses to excessive stimulation and self-recovery, closely resembling that of biological nociceptors. The device exhibits neurapraxia-like responses with a recovery time of only 40 s. The experimentally obtained synaptic characteristics are further employed in a device-aware fully connected artificial neural network, yielding a handwritten digit recognition accuracy of 97.9%. Various investigations on the dynamics of charge transport have revealed trap-assisted hopping through transient localization, which is induced by shallow and deep traps. The integration of artificial nociception and pattern recognition in a highly stable low-power synaptic device demonstrates the potential of the hybrid memristor for multifunctional neuromorphic hardware.

title: Magnetic Fe/Cu Metal–Organic Frameworks-Derived Trilayer Cathode for Enhanced Enrofloxacin Degradation in Heterogeneous Electro-Fenton via Synergistic Radical and Nonradical Pathways
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous electro-Fenton (HEF) technology represents a promising eco-friendly strategy for wastewater remediation. However, sluggish Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling and reliance on a single hydroxyl radical (•OH) pathway limit its overall catalytic efficiency and oxidant utilization. Herein, a bifunctional trilayer cathode (Fe8Cu2@C-GF/ACF) was fabricated by integrating activated carbon fiber (ACF) with a magnetic Fe/Cu metal–organic frameworks-derived layer grown on graphite felt. This architecture spatially couples H2O2 electrogeneration with immediate activation, maximizing the effective utilization of generated oxidants. Furthermore, Cu incorporation thermodynamically accelerates Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling. The bimetallic synergy facilitates the simultaneous generation of radical (•OH) and nonradical (1O2) species. Quenching and EPR analyses confirmed these dual pathways collectively accelerate enrofloxacin (ENRO) degradation. The system achieves excellent mineralization across a broad initial pH range (3.0 to 9.0). Crucially, effective operation at neutral pH eliminates the need for chemical adjustment. Specifically, treating 100 mg L−1 ENRO at initial pH 7.0 and 18 mA cm−2 yielded a 75.6% mineralization degree. Degradation intermediates were elucidated via DFT calculations and UPLC-QqQ-MS analysis. Finally, the cathode exhibits high stability and low metal leaching. Its intrinsic magnetic recoverability prevents secondary solid waste and promotes practical material reuse for sustainable water treatment.

title: Dynamic Energy-Dissipating Interface Design Reconciles Thermal Performance with Interfacial Reliability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Highly filled thermal interface materials (TIMs) are essential for reliable heat dissipation in high-power electronics, yet restricted polymer chain mobility and reduced interfacial conformability make it difficult to achieve high thermal conductivity, strong adhesion, and crack-growth resistance simultaneously. We propose a dynamic energy-dissipating interface (DEDI) strategy that coordinates favorable interfacial affinity, stable chemical anchoring, and dynamic bulk energy dissipation to improve interfacial stability and crack resistance in highly filled TIMs. γ-Methacryloxypropyl trimethoxysilane (γ-MPS) provides stable chemical anchoring at the substrate interface, while urethane-associated polar interactions contribute to favorable interfacial affinity. Reversible disulfide and hydrogen-bond interactions within the bulk network promote deformation accommodation and mechanical energy dissipation. Surface-modified Al2O3/ZnO hybrid fillers form a multiscale network that provides efficient heat-transfer pathways. The resulting PSM-60-1.2 exhibits a thermal conductivity of 3.88 W·m−1·K−1, an adhesion strength of 4.25 MPa, and an adhesion energy of 3080.04 J·m−2. Combined experimental and finite-element analyses support coordinated interfacial stabilization, bulk energy dissipation, and enhanced thermomechanical deformation accommodation. After 100 thermal shock cycles between −40 and 150 °C, PSM-60-1.2 shows a 6.0 °C increase in maximum steady-state temperature, compared with 16.2 °C for the commercial thermally conductive adhesive, with less interfacial cracking and low-viscosity liquid infiltration. The DEDI design offers a molecular strategy for combining high thermal conductivity, high adhesion energy, and long-term thermomechanical reliability in highly filled TIMs.

title: Ultrastable 4.99 V Li rich Mn-based cathodes achieved by catalytic-shielded and strain-buffered interface engineering
abstract: Lithium-rich manganese-based layered oxides (LROs) offer high theoretical capacity but are limited by irreversible oxygen redox, voltage fade, and structural degradation upon cycling. Herein, we develop a dual-interface engineering strategy for LRO cathodes, integrating a catalytic-shielded carbon coating and interface-confined discrete spinel domains. The carbon layer decouples electrolyte decomposition from lattice-driven catalysis, suppressing cathode-electrolyte interphase growth and oxygen release, while subsurface-confined spinel phases establish three-dimensional Li+ transport pathways and mitigate lattice strain. title: IMAN: An Integrated Colorimetric Sensor for Direct Detection of PD-L1 on Extracellular Vesicles in Lung Cancer Diagnosis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lung cancer is a leading cause of cancer mortality, yet early diagnosis remains difficult, highlighting the need for sensitive, noninvasive methods. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) and their surface proteins (e.g., PD-L1) are promising biomarkers; nevertheless, current EV detection requires time-consuming purification, sophisticated instrumentation, and long measurement protocols, resulting in high expenses and operational difficulties. This study developed an integrated colorimetric sensor, IMAN, based on a strategy of “Immunomagnetic Microbeads (IM) capture + Aptamer(Apt) recognition + Nanozyme (N) catalysis”. IMAN employs magnetic beads modified with antibodies against CD9 and CD81 to directly capture EVs from serum, eliminating the need for time-consuming prior isolation; combined with a one-step colorimetric readout, the entire workflow can be completed with only ∼40 min of hands-on time, requiring no complex instrumentation. The PD-L1 protein on the EV surface is specifically recognized by a nanoparticle-bound nucleic acid aptamer. Signal generation is achieved through the catalytic oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) by a platinum-gold bimetallic nanozyme (Pt@Au). The facile IMAN colorimetric method demonstrated a relatively broad dynamic range (107–1010 particles/mL), high specificity (unaffected by 100 pg/mL soluble PD-L1 in serum), and reproducibility (relative standard deviation, RSD = 9.1%). Analysis of clinical serum samples revealed significantly elevated EV-PD-L1 levels in patients with lung cancer compared with healthy donors and patients with benign nodule (p < 0.01). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis yielded areas under the curve (AUC) of 0.849 for distinguishing patients with lung cancer from healthy donors and 0.860 for distinguishing patients with lung cancer from patients with benign nodules, which are superior to those of the conventional serum biomarkers CEA and Cyfra21-1. By addressing the cost, complexity, and slow response of current methods, IMAN offers a simple, cost-effective platform for direct EV surface protein detection without complex instrumentation, providing a novel tool for the noninvasive lung cancer diagnosis.

title: High-Performance SrLiAl3N4:Eu2+ Red Phosphor via Alloy Precursor Synthesis for Laser-Driven and Wide-Gamut Displays
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract In this work, the alloy-precursor solid-state synthesis strategy (AS-method) is employed to fabricate high-performance SrLiAl3N4:Eu2+ phosphors. This approach effectively suppresses the oxidation of Eu2+ to Eu3+ compared to conventional solid-state synthesis (S-method). The resultant optimization of the local structure not only enhances the structural rigidity but also modulates the surrounding chemical pressure at different activator sites. This site-selective regulation leads to spectral narrowing and a blue shift in the emission. The optimized phosphor exhibits an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 52.38%, a value that ranks among the highest reported for the SLA-based phosphors. Furthermore, it demonstrates an ultrahigh saturation threshold of 90.69 W/mm2 under blue laser excitation, surpassing most reported red phosphors. When applied in white LEDs, it achieves 104% of the NTSC color gamut. Thus, this phosphor indicates great potential for applications in both laser-driven and high-color-gamut displays.

title: Synergistic Interfacial Engineering in V2C MXene Heterostructures for Enhanced Nano-aluminum Reactivity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nano-aluminum (nano-Al) is a high-energy-density material with exceptional reactivity, making it promising for aerospace and military applications. Reducing particle size increases the active surface area and interfacial mass diffusion, but intrinsic agglomeration and dense alumina shells hinder diffusion. Conventional additives often reduce reactivity. Here, we modulate nano-Al interfacial diffusion through synergistic interactions in a V2C MXene heterostructure. The self-assembly of nano-Al on MXene suppresses agglomeration, while fluorine-containing terminations etch the alumina shells. The heterostructure also forms metal oxide contact layers that promote solid-phase thermite reactions. These effects increase the peak heat flow in air to 107.6 W g−1, 3.5 times that of pristine nano-Al. Solid-phase reactions complete energy release before Al melting, minimizing energy loss. The composite shows larger flame areas and a lower minimum ignition concentration (≥5 wt %). Adjusting the heating temperature reduces the total combustion duration by 88.9% and increases the dynamic pressure. This versatile fabrication process enables tunable performance for diverse operational environments.

title: Controlled Interfacial Electronic Coupling in Chemical Vapor Deposition-Grown WSe2 Monolayers on Au(111)
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report on the controlled growth and interface engineering of high-quality WSe2 monolayers on Au(111) using ambient-pressure chemical vapor deposition (CVD) combined with comprehensive surface-sensitive characterization in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV). The as-grown films exhibit a selenium buffer layer, which enables the formation of a weakly coupled WSe2 phase at the metal interface, as revealed by scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and low-energy electron diffraction (LEED). Annealing in UHV removes the selenium buffer layer and leads to the emergence of a pronounced moiré superstructure and a transition toward a strongly coupled WSe2 phase. Furthermore, this transformation is accompanied by pronounced modifications of the electronic structure, including phase-dependent changes in the valence band structure observed by angle-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy (ARPES), a hybridization-induced metallization measured by scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), and a significant decrease in the work function determined by field emission resonance (FER) and ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy (UPS). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirm strong WSe2–Au hybridization and the presence of the mid-gap states for the strongly coupled phase, whereas the Se8 buffer layer weakens the interaction of WSe2 with Au, so that its electronic structure is close to that for the freestanding system. Our results demonstrate that growth-induced interface chemistry provides a powerful handle to tune the electronic coupling in WSe2/Au(111), establishing a direct link between interfacial structure and electronic properties in metal–transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) interfaces.

title: Improvement of Photocatalytic and Nanomechanical Properties of GaN Nanowires via Core-Shell Surface Modification
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The practical implementation of photocatalytic water splitting for sustainable hydrogen production is largely limited by the efficiency of the oxygen evolution reaction at the photoanode. Gallium nitride is a promising material for photoanode fabrication, provided that suitable nanostructuring strategies are applied to enhance its efficiency and stability. Here, we report the functionalization of gallium nitride nanowires with a 5 nm-thick titanium dioxide layer of and a 10 nm biomimetic polydopamine coating, resulting in a 1.9-fold (190%) increase in the anodic photocurrent, as demonstrated by chronoamperometry. We provide a detailed explanation of this enhancement based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and a series of optical studies. The observed decrease in photoluminescence intensity (60–90%) and shortening of carrier lifetimes from 0.17 to 0.07 ns correlate with the improved photocatalytic performance. Moreover, the 50% reduction in the band-to-band to defect emission ratio and the analysis of exciton recombination pathways show the role of defect-related and surface recombination processes in determining the photocatalytic activity of the nanowires. The enhanced photocatalytic performance is further attributed to shell deposition, which induces surface-state passivation, band realignment, and the quantum-confined Stark effect. Concurrently, changes in strain distribution are confirmed by increased heterogeneity of the GaN E2high phonon mode frequency distribution, expressed by an increase in the standard deviation from 0.09 up to 0.17 cm–1 and linewidth broadening from 3.2 up to 3.4 cm–1, as observed by Raman spectroscopy. Additionally, we show that the nanomechanical properties of the nanowires are significantly improved after shell deposition, by the elimination of pop-in events, enhanced elastic recovery, and an increase in Young’s modulus from 12 to 37 GPa. Finally, we point out opportunities for further optimization of similarly functionalized nanowire systems to achieve even higher efficiencies and support emerging applications.

title: Modelling and Emulation of Afferent-Like Excitatory–Inhibitory Spiking Using Ovonic Threshold Devices for Neuromorphic Oscillatory Computing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Spike-based computing has attracted increasing attention for efficient information processing, creating demand for neuromorphic hardware capable of generating and processing spikes. Ovonic threshold switching (OTS) devices are promising spiking neurons because their threshold-switching behavior and negative differential resistance enable compact spike-generation circuits, while their scalability supports dense integration. However, a circuit-level design framework linking defect dynamics with conduction behavior remains lacking. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an intensity-tuned artificial neuron based on a GeAsTe OTS device integrated with a resistor-capacitor (RC) circuit. The neuron shows a non-monotonic excitatory–self-inhibitory response with applied voltage, phenomenologically analogous to excitatory–inhibitory behavior in biological neurons. The spiking frequency initially increases and then decreases beyond an inflection voltage point. This transition arises intrinsically from competition between RC charging dynamics and conductive filament retention in the OTS device, rather than from a separate inhibitory pathway. The neuron achieves a spiking frequency of up to 1.6 MHz. The behavior is supported by simulations using a dynamical model for diffusive filament-based memristors, accounting for resistance changes from filament formation and rupture. Furthermore, a physics-informed compact SPICE model combining defect-state transitions and filament evolution reproduces OTS switching and predicts neuron dynamics under varying temperatures, internal resistances, and circuit conditions. Finally, circuit simulations of a coupled OTS neuron network demonstrate vertex coloring with phase convergence within approximately 5 μs, highlighting the potential of this framework for compact, energy-efficient brain-inspired computing.

title: Surface and Electronic-Structure Regulation of NiCrPt-LDH for Ampere-Level Methanol-Assisted Hydrogen Production in Alkaline Seawater
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Substituting the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) with the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) provides an energy-saving route for alkaline seawater electrolysis, but it demands bifunctional electrodes that efficiently facilitate both anodic MOR and cathodic hydrogen evolution reactions (HER) in chloride-containing alkaline media. This work reports a surface and electronic-structure regulation strategy for a low-Pt (0.86 wt %) NiCrPt-LDH electrode constructed on nickel foam via a single-step hydrothermal route. The NiCrPt-LDH electrode integrates an open nanosheet framework, a defect-enriched metal–oxygen surface environment, and a super-hydrophilic/-aerophobic interface, which requires only 74, 146, and 228 mV to deliver 100, 500, and 1000 mA cm–2 for HER, respectively, with 1380 h of stability at 500 mA cm–2. Its Pt-mass-normalized HER activity is much higher than that of commercial Pt/C. For MOR in methanol-containing alkaline seawater, NiCrPt-LDH reaches 100 mA cm–2 under an applied potential of 1.401 V vs RHE. The NiCrPt-LDH (+) || NiCrPt-LDH (–) electrolyzer outputs 100 mA cm–2 at an operating voltage of 1.477 V, underscoring the potential of low-platinum, surface-engineered bifunctional LDH electrodes for methanol-assisted hydrogen production in alkaline seawater electrolysis.

title: High- k Gate Dielectrics for Organic Field-Effect Transistors: Interfacial Engineering, Performance Optimization, and Scalable Flexible Electronics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organic field-effect transistors (OFETs) are promising platforms for flexible, wearable, biointegrated, and large-area electronics owing to their mechanical compliance, solution processability, low-temperature fabrication, and molecular tunability. However, their practical application requires low-voltage operation, low power consumption, high operational stability, and scalable manufacturing, which are strongly influenced by the gate dielectric and its interface with the organic semiconductor. High-k gate dielectrics can increase gate capacitance and enhance electrostatic control, enabling low-voltage operation. However, a higher dielectric constant does not necessarily lead to better device performance, as strong polarization, surface polarity, interfacial trapping, dipolardisorder, remote phonon scattering, leakage, ion migration, and dielectric–semiconductor incompatibility can impair charge transport and device reliability. This Review presents a performance-oriented and interface-centered overview of high-k gate dielectrics for OFETs. We first classify high-k dielectric systems into inorganic oxides, molecularly engineered polymers, organic–inorganic hybrids and composites, and all-organic composite/multilayer structures, highlighting their polarization mechanisms, advantages, limitations, and structure–property relationships. We then discuss how dielectric properties and interfaces affect carrier mobility, threshold voltage, switching characteristics, charge injection, leakage current, hysteresis, and operational stability. Particular attention is given to interface engineering strategies, including surface modification, buffer layers, multilayer architectures, molecular design, composite construction, and defect/passivation control. We further discuss long-term reliability under electrical, thermal, mechanical, and environmental stresses, as well as emerging dielectric systems, low-temperature and scalable fabrication, large-area uniformity, process integration, and commercialization challenges. Finally, we summarize key design considerations for balancing high capacitance, low leakage, interfacial compatibility, mechanical robustness, environmental stability, and scalable processability. By integrating dielectric design, interface engineering, device physics, reliability, and manufacturing, this Review provides guidelines for developing low-voltage, stable, and scalable OFETs for next-generation flexible electronics.

title: Three-Dimensional-Printed Lithium-Doped Conductive Carbon@Hydroxyapatite Scaffolds for Coordinated Neurovascular-Osseous Regeneration
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The repair of critical-sized bone defects remains a formidable clinical challenge, where coordinated neurovascular reconstruction is important for effective bone regeneration. Accordingly, this study aimed to develop a three-dimensional (3D)-printed hydroxyapatite (HAp) scaffold integrating a polydopamine (PDA)-derived conductive carbon interface with Li+ release, and to evaluate its neural-, vascular-, and osteogenic-related effects in vitro and its bone-regenerative performance in vivo. A lithium-containing, hydrothermally carbonized HAp scaffold (HAp@C/Li) was fabricated through 3D printing, Li+-assisted dopamine coating, and hydrothermal carbonization. Material characterization confirmed a PDA-derived carbon coating with measurable local surface conductivity and Li+ release characterized by an early release phase followed by a gradual plateau. In vitro experimental results revealed that HAp@C/Li possessed excellent cytocompatibility. It effectively promoted neurite outgrowth of dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons, migration and tube formation of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs), as well as osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). In vivo evaluation in a rat femoral condyle defect model showed favorable bone repair, collagen deposition, vascular remodeling, and neural-associated tissue responses, with significantly higher BMD at 8 weeks, whereas BV/TV did not differ significantly from that of the HAp group. Collectively, these results indicate that the HAp@C/Li scaffold provides a promising therapeutic strategy for the clinical repair of critical-sized bone defects.

title: Vicinal Functional-Group Engineering in Defect-Engineered MOFs for One-Step Ethylene Purification
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of C2H6-selective adsorbents offers a promising strategy for energy-efficient C2H4 purification from C2H6/C2H4 mixtures. However, the similar physicochemical properties of C2H6 and C2H4 make it challenging to achieve preferential adsorption of C2H6. Herein, we propose a vicinal functional-group engineering strategy to construct C2H6-recognition domains, enabling efficient one-step C2H4 purification from C2H6/C2H4 mixtures. The adjacent functional groups on the modulators are introduced close to the defect sites of MOFs, constructing synergistic electrostatic-confinement microenvironments for C2H6 recognition. The fluorinated-defective MOF (UiO-66-(CF3)2) exhibits C2H6 preferential adsorption with an uptake of 2.2 mmol/g at 298 K and 100 kPa. Breakthrough experiments further confirm the dynamic separation performance of UiO-66-(CF3)2, achieving high-purity C2H4 (>99.99 %) with a productivity of 12.67 L/kg. Theoretical calculations further reveal that the adjacent functional groups in the ligands would induce electrostatic potential redistribution and confined pore structures, strengthening C2H6 adsorption on defective MOF over C2H4. This work establishes a vicinal functional-group engineering strategy for constructing synergistic electrostatic-confinement microenvironments toward C2H6 recognition in MOFs.

title: Molecular Architecture of Covalent Adaptable Network Additives Governs Their Integration into Melt-Processed Polyamide 6
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) are predominantly developed as bulk thermoset matrices, while their use as dynamically crosslinked functional phases within melt-processed thermoplastics remains largely unexplored. Here, phosphorus-containing CANs (P-CANs) with systematically varied molecular architectures are employed as macromolecular additives in polyamide 6 (PA6) to establish relationships between network structure, dynamic response, dispersion, retention, and melt processability. Transitioning from a rigid small-molecule-derived network to flexible polyphosphonate architectures shifted the glass-transition temperature from 160 to –5 °C and markedly altered stress relaxation and deformation under processing conditions. These architecture-dependent differences translated directly into thermoplastic integration: the rigid P-CAN formed larger phosphorus-rich domains and exhibited greater phosphorus retention, whereas the most flexible network appeared more uniformly dispersed, lowered processing resistance, and promoted shear-thinning behavior. The resulting balance between dispersion and retention enabled kilogram-scale twin-screw compounding and continuous film extrusion of homogeneous PA6 composites containing 5–10 wt % flexible P-CAN. Despite low final phosphorus contents (∼0.25–0.60 wt %), incorporation of the P-CANs increased limiting oxygen index, promoted char formation, and reduced microscale heat release. These results demonstrate that CAN molecular architecture provides a tunable design parameter for controlling the integration and functional performance of dynamically crosslinked polymeric additives in melt-processed thermoplastics.

title: In Situ Activated Bi2WO6 Nanosheets with Fast-Response and Self-Bleaching Electrochromism for Automotive Antiglare Rearview Mirrors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Trailing vehicle headlight glare critically endangers nighttime driving safety, with electrochromic devices (ECDs) being the most promising solution. Nevertheless, commercial organic electrochromic materials face high cost and irreversible degradation, whereas inorganic alternatives exhibit slow response and severe memory effect, severely restricting their application in antiglare rearview mirrors. Herein, we report the electrochromic behavior of thin bismuth tungstate (T-BWO) nanosheets synthesized via a facile hydrothermal method. A unique in situ activation process is discovered, accompanied by (19.7 ± 1.8)% leaching of surface Bi atoms and a transient dark transition state, which endows the activated T-BWO with exceptional electrochromic performance: an ultralow working voltage window of –0.6/0.3 V, ultrafast coloration/bleaching times of (0.81 ± 0.06)/(0.55 ± 0.04) s, a high coloration efficiency of (148.3 ± 7.8) cm2 C–1, and reasonably fast self-bleaching under open-circuit conditions. The assembled T-BWO-based self-bleaching ECD delivers a moderate optical modulation (ΔR) of (37.8 ± 1.7)% and excellent cycling stability (86% performance retention after 900 cycles). This work not only introduces a novel high-performance inorganic electrochromic material but also provides a new design paradigm for functional ECDs toward practical automotive antiglare applications.

title: Economic and emissions analysis of natural gas power with high-efficiency CO2 capture
Climate-reliable power systems via stochastic programming with scenarios generated with a posteriori time aggregation
abstract: The decarbonization of power systems requires managing intermittent renewable generation and climate variability while ensuring social welfare and reliability. However, incorporating extensive climate datasets into optimization models to capture variability compromises tractability, uncertainty traceability, or reliability. We propose a novel framework for climate-reliable power system design that integrates a bi-criteria a posteriori aggregation technique with a stochastic program that incorporates operational scenarios with a non-uniform number of representative days. This scenario construction enables efficient representation of extreme weather events while maintaining computational feasibility. To benchmark the framework, capacity portfolios are optimized separately for each climate dataset, distinguishing between climate scenario and climate model uncertainty. The approach is demonstrated using 47 climate projections for Saudi Arabia by 2050 under two policy settings: a 100 million tonnes of CO 2 emissions target and a fully renewable system. Results indicate substantial cost dispersion across climate models within the same emissions scenario, reaching up to 40% in the fully renewable system under the RCP4.5 climate scenario. Strong economic incentives for climate change mitigation are identified, primarily driven by the high sensitivity of electricity demand to rising temperatures. Uncertainty-aware designs with the proposed approach yield 3–6% higher design costs than single-climate designs. However, cross-scenario assessment reveals substantial supply shortfalls and excess emissions for single-climate designs, with potential additional costs that are at least 2.6 times the additional investment required by the proposed framework. Compared with stochastic programs having a uniform number of representative days, the proposed approach achieves lower unserved energy and lower worst-case evaluation costs with comparable total computational effort, demonstrating its value for climate-aware power system planning.

Dual-Microstructure Configuration Design Enabling Highly Sensitive Biotemplated Flexible Capacitive Pressure Sensors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Flexible capacitive pressure sensors (FCPSs) that resolve subtle pressure are central to soft robotics and human health monitoring. Their sensitivity is affected by microstructures incorporated at the interface between the electrode and dielectric layers, but fabricating fine artificial microstructures typically requires costly techniques. Biological templates offer a cost-effective way to form these microstructures, yet biotemplated FCPSs have remained limited in sensitivity. Efforts to improve sensitivity have predominantly focused on microstructure geometries, whereas the microstructure configuration in the sensor has not been well-studied. Here, we establish design insights for microstructure configurations through simplified computational analysis, revealing that amplifying the effective interelectrode distance variation rate and effective permittivity variation rate within the structured region is the key to enhancing overall sensitivity. Following this insight, we propose a dual-microstructure configuration that increases the air fraction within the structured region, leading to the amplified effective permittivity variation rate. Both computational and experimental assessments demonstrate that the dual-microstructure configuration outperforms conventional ones in sensitivity, with the fabricated sensor achieving the highest sensitivity of 4.3 kPa–1 among all the reported biotemplated FCPSs using the same dielectric materials (Table S1), along with a fast response/recovery time of 46/20 ms, a low detection limit of 1.2 Pa, and stable operation over 7500 cycles. These performance attributes enable the sensor for applications in robotic hand tactile sensing for soft objects and real-time physiological signal monitoring. Consequently, the proposed dual-microstructure configuration offers a generalizable pathway to enhance the sensitivity of biotemplated FCPSs, promoting the development of high-performance, cost-effective flexible pressure sensors.

abstract: Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, population growth, and fast economic expansion have made emerging economies significant contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.
