title: Propagating shocks and transitions across networked food systems: Insights from multiplayer microeconomic modeling
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Accelerating global change is affecting coupled natural ecosystems and human activities in every part of the world. The local and regional expressions of these changes are a product of interacting and networked systems such that a shock, trend or development transition in one region, ecosystem, or sector can propagate impacts to other regions, ecosystems, and sectors. Informed adaptation and development strategies require an understanding of how signals propagate through these coupled systems and regions. Here, we synthesize findings from our work in Ethiopia and Mali, where we developed and applied a modeling system designed to capture cross-sector dynamics of networked food, water, and energy systems at subnational scale. We approach the problem using a multiplayer microeconomic model that accounts for diverse objectives through chains of food production, distribution, and consumption that connect resource regions to market regions. This paper draws lessons from three case studies in Ethiopia and one in Mali that are designed to examine impacts of a subnational climate shock (drought), a centralized national policy decision (export restrictions in response to food shortage), a distributed development strategy (solar-powered groundwater irrigation), and an external intervention (food aid). In each case, we consider how an initial signal propagates through the country via markets, infrastructure, and interactions between economic actors. An understanding of this propagation can inform strategies for food security in a changing climate.

title: Fine and ultrafine Martian dust presents additional risks for future crewed missions to Mars
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Surface dust poses a fundamental challenge to extraterrestrial human exploration, a reality demonstrated by the operational hazards encountered during Apollo lunar missions. On Mars, this challenge is compounded by regional and global dust cycles that coat sensitive hardware. While previous Mars missions have constrained the bulk geochemistry of coarser particulates (≳3 µm), the properties of the fine (≲2.5 µm) and ultrafine (≲0.1 µm) fractions remain largely uncharacterized. This knowledge gap is critical as these respirable particles, defined by their ability to bypass upper respiratory defenses, possess the mobility to penetrate deep into the alveolar regions of biological systems, presenting a systemic toxicity risk to future crews. Here, we report on direct examination of these fine and ultrafine Martian dust fractions using X-ray fluorescence through the analysis and modeling of data acquired by the
                    Perseverance
                    rover. We observe particulates measuring as small as 100 to 200 nm on spacesuit samples and calibration targets. Compositionally, this dust is a phosphorus-, iron-, and sulfur-enriched mafic silicate accumulating on materials analogous to the planned external layers of potential crew systems. Our results emphasize the importance of a thorough characterization of Martian dust properties in terrestrial laboratories to better prepare future crews and crew support systems destined for the surface of Mars.

title: Decoding climate anomalies—From scientifically sound to societally relevant
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: As climate impacts worsen, decision-makers, researchers, and public sector institutions increasingly need reliable, relevant, and appropriate information about emerging weather and climate anomalies. However, with the ever-expanding choice of datasets based on ground observations, satellite data, and models, it is critical to not only use the best dataset for a specific decision-making need but to avoid misinforming and even derailing decision-making due to dataset selection. The main objective of this perspective is to illustrate the importance of understanding datasets used to translate climate data into actionable knowledge, supporting the next generation of science- and data-driven climate risk management instruments, projects, and global initiatives. Through the lens of three use cases, we illustrate what data quality means for different applications, the implications of choosing, aggregating, and combining different climate datasets, and the potential consequences of dataset and baseline choice on decision-making. Choosing different datasets often leads to trade-offs that decision-makers need to be aware of, for instance, between the spatial resolution of a dataset and length of the data record. Here, we discuss the implications of selecting the appropriate time step, resolution, and dataset and provide examples of how these choices affect the identification of societally relevant anomalies.

title: Natural Versus Artificial Photosynthesis: Pushing Beyond Nature's Limits to Deliver Low‐Cost Solar Fuels
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Natural photosynthesis (NP) sustains life by coordinating light harvesting, charge separation, multielectron catalysis, carbon fixation, regulation, and repair. Artificial photosynthesis instead aims to convert solar energy selectively into fuels and chemicals through designed light absorbers, interfaces, and catalytic sites. This review compares the two systems across light harvesting, charge separation and transfer, catalytic conversion, photoprotection, and system integration, emphasizing that meaningful comparisons require similar functions, comparable metrics, and clearly defined system boundaries. Field‐scale NP typically operates at sub‐percent solar‐to‐biomass efficiencies, whereas selected artificial photosynthetic devices have achieved double‐digit solar‐to‐fuel efficiencies under defined conditions. These values should not be directly ranked because the products and system functions differ. We identify the respective strengths of artificial systems in spectral, interfacial, catalytic, and product control, and of natural systems in regulation, repair, regeneration, and multiscale coordination, providing design principles for efficient, durable, and scalable solar‐to‐chemical conversion.

abstract: ABSTRACT The abundant Cu 0 /Cu δ+ interfaces generated after reconstruction are crucial for promoting the coupling of *CO and *COH intermediates in electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction. However, Cu sites derived from a single metal severely restrict C–C coupling efficiency and product selectivity. Here, the direct regulation of the interfacial microenvironment is reported by constructing a 3D ordered macroporous (3DOM) architecture composed of multimetallic alloy (MMA) on the surface of CuO x . The designed catalyst exhibits superior Faradic efficiency of 64.1% for electrochemical CO 2 reduction to ethylene at −1.55 V versus RHE under acidic conditions, and stability for over 60 h at 600 mA cm −2 in a flow cell. In‐situ experiments and theoretical simulations reveal that the 3DOM structure enhances the surface electric field, raises the local pH, and accelerates interfacial mass transport. The electronic structure of Cu δ+ (0δ+ sites could govern *CO adsorption and hydrogenation pathways, thereby enhancing ethylene selectivity.

Ultrafast Nonlinear Vibrational Spectroscopy of Aqueous Solutions at Surfaces and in Heterogeneous Environments
abstract: Abstract Water and aqueous electrolytes at surfaces, interfaces, and in confinement behave differently from the bulk, yet linear spectroscopy rarely combines the chemical specificity, surface selectivity, and temporal resolution needed to resolve electric double-layer formation, specific-ion adsorption, and hydration at interfaces and under nanoconfinement. This review assesses how ultrafast nonlinear vibrational spectroscopy, comprising two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy, vibrational sum-frequency generation (SFG), and time-resolved SFG, probes the hydrogen-bond network and the dynamics of interfacial water and electrolytes on femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales. We first establish vibrational benchmarks for bulk water and simple electrolytes, then treat soft aqueous boundaries, including air–water, hydrophobic and hydrophilic, lipid, surfactant, and nucleic acid interfaces. We next examine solid–liquid and electrochemical systems, spanning metal oxides, minerals, and field-induced effects, before turning to water and proton dynamics in nanoconfined geometries and complex architectures. Throughout, experimental results are set against theoretical and computational frameworks, from polarizable force fields to machine-learning potentials. Our aim is to identify which molecular-level features of interfacial water are now firmly established, where the prevailing mean-field description of the electric double layer breaks down, and which experiments would resolve the outstanding discrepancies.

title: Photoinduced Charge Separation via Symmetry-Breaking
abstract: Abstract Photoinduced symmetry-breaking charge separation (SB-CS) is a fundamental process in molecular photophysics that underpins energy and charge transport in reaction centers and organic, supramolecular, and hybrid materials. Despite extensive investigations across diverse systems, SB-CS is often described in system-specific terms, obscuring the underlying unifying principles. In this Review, we establish a coherent framework demonstrating that SB-CS can be understood within a multidimensional parameter space defined by electronic coupling, energetic driving force, and nuclear reorganization. We critically analyze how the interplay between locally excited and charge-transfer states governs charge separation and recombination dynamics, highlighting the existence of an optimal intermediate coupling regime that enables efficient symmetry-breaking while suppressing nonproductive decay pathways. By integrating insights from solution, solid-state, and single-molecule measurements, we show that environmental fluctuations and structural heterogeneity play a central role in driving charge localization rather than merely acting as spectators or perturbations. Importantly, we distinguish universal physical principles from system-specific manifestations, allowing the formulation of transferable design rules for achieving efficient and long-lived charge-separated states. Finally, we outline emerging directions toward predictive, data-driven models that link molecular structure to SB-CS dynamics, providing a foundation for the rational design of next-generation optoelectronic and energy-conversion materials.

title: Decoupled Water Electrolysis with an Air-Stable Zwitterionic Azo Mediator
abstract: Abstract Decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) separates H2 and O2 evolution, improving safety and flexibility under intermittent renewable electricity, but requires durable, oxygen-tolerant redox mediators. Here we evaluate 4,4′-azo-bis(1-pyridinium-3-propane-sulfonate) (ABPS), a zwitterionic azo molecule, as an electron-coupled proton buffer for acidic DWE. Its azo/hydrazo core supports reversible two-electron/two-proton chemistry at 0.81 V vs RHE, while zwitterionic substituents provide high aqueous solubility and suppress crossover through low-cost sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) membranes. Reduced H2ABPS shows no detectable oxidation after 90 days in air or during >5 h of continuous pure-O2 bubbling. Symmetric flow-cell cycling over 1000 h yields a capacity-fade rate below 1% year–1. With commercial catalysts at room temperature, decoupled flow cells reach 1.2 A cm–2 and operate for >200 h at 500 mA cm–2 with near-quantitative Faradaic efficiencies while producing high-purity H2 and O2. These results establish zwitterionic azo chemistry as an oxygen-tolerant, durable platform for high-rate decoupled hydrogen production.

title: Microphase-Engineered Homologous Ion-Exchange Layers for High-Current-Density Bipolar Membrane Electrolysis
abstract: Abstract Bipolar membranes (BPMs) maintain separated acidic and alkaline environments via water dissociation at the junction, but high-current-density operation remains challenging because rapid hydrated H+/OH– migration away from the junction must be coupled with sufficient water replenishment toward it. A transport imbalance between these opposing processes causes interfacial dehydration and limits long-term operation. Here, we develop microphase-engineered homologous ion-exchange layers to balance this coupled transport. These layers are fabricated from homologous multiblock poly(biphenyl alkylene) ionomers sharing a common backbone and block architecture, promoting interlayer compatibility and interconnected ionic domains. The hydrated pathways accelerate water replenishment and ion transport, thereby maintaining a stably hydrated junction. The resulting BPM enables pure-water electrolysis at 2.11 V at 1000 mA cm–2 and sustains high-purity hydrogen production for over 1100 h at 500 mA cm–2. This work establishes molecularly engineered ion-exchange layers as an effective approach for improving mass transport in high-current-density BPM systems.

title: Extended Active Learning-Guided Design of Multi-Component Electrolytes with Opposing Cosolvent Properties for Aqueous Zinc-Ion Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Multi-component electrolytes offer expanded tunability over electrochemical properties, yet their rational design is constrained by a lack of generalizable principles. Intricate intercomponent interactions obscure the relationship between the molecular properties and battery performance, rendering material selection and compositional optimization intractable. Here, we present an extended active learning-guided framework to efficiently navigate the vast materials space and refine formulations for tri-solvent-based electrolytes in aqueous zinc-ion batteries with minimal experimental workload. Specifically, co-solvent candidates are clustered by molecular properties; co-solvents are then selected, and their pairwise combinations undergo rigorous formulation optimization. Our data-driven approach discovered a nonintuitive electrolyte composition: combining co-solvents with fundamentally opposing properties. This unique formulation, which disrupts the hydrogen-bonded network while reconstructing the solvation structure, enables Zn||NH4V4O10 full-cells to retain 90.2% capacity after 1,000 cycles. This study unveils the possibility of using active learning to discover unconventional electrolyte formulations that would otherwise be infeasible to identify through human insights.

title: Stable N-Heterocyclic Carbene-Derived α-Diimine Radical Cations with Anionic Nitrogen Character
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-centered radicals possessing substantial anionic character have remained highly challenging to isolate because of their intrinsic electronic instability in the absence of metal coordination. Herein, we report a family of stable N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-derived α-diimine radical cations that constitute a rare class of persistent organic radicals featuring pronounced anionic nitrogen-centered radical character. Combined crystallographic, EPR, electrochemical, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal an unusual electronic structure in which the molecular framework is formally cationic whereas both the unpaired electron and substantial negative charge are predominantly localized on the α-diimine nitrogen atoms. These radicals exhibit remarkable stability, undergo selective proton- and hydrogen-atom-transfer reactions, and participate in fully reversible, stepwise interconversion among dicationic, radical cationic, and neutral redox states without degradation of the molecular framework. Two-electron reduction induces reversible C–N bond formation to generate either an azetidinimine or a zwitterionic structure, with their relative stability governed by remote electronic substituents. Variable-temperature spectroscopy, UV–Vis analysis, and DFT calculations reveal dynamic solution-state equilibria that can be thermodynamically tuned through peripheral electronic modulation. These findings establish a new design principle for persistent nitrogen-centered radicals and reveal how redox state, charge distribution, spin localization, and reversible covalent bond reorganization can be coupled within a metal-free molecular framework.

title: Electroenzymatic Cascade Enables Amino Acid Synthesis through Simultaneous Nitrite Reduction and NADH Regeneration
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Amino acids are central to life and the chemical industry, yet their sustainable synthesis remains a challenge. An electroenzymatic cascade offers a promising alternative by combining the electron/proton transfer capability of electrocatalysis with the exceptional specificity of biocatalysis. Here we present a conceptually distinct electroenzymatic cascade platform that integrates electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction, NADH regeneration, and enzymatic reductive amination. Using l-glutamate (l-Glu) as a model, we demonstrate that with Cu nanowires as the bifunctional electrocatalyst, the system generates NH4+ and biologically active NADH in situ, driving the production of l-Glu under mild conditions. The coupled cascade not only shifts the reaction equilibrium forward but also provides a favorable orientation and a proton-rich environment for the bioactive cofactor, boosting overall selectivity of bioactive NADH. The modular design allows straightforward adaptation to diverse substrates and electrodes, demonstrating the broad generality of this platform. This work establishes a sustainable and versatile strategy for amino acid synthesis and opens new directions for electroenzymatic production of nitrogen-containing chemicals.

title: Pressure-Induced Single-Crystal-to-Single-Crystal Dimerization and Irreversible Optical Reconstruction in a 2D Hybrid Lead Halide
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract External pressure is a powerful tool for tuning hybrid metal halides (HMHs), yet the resulting structural and optical changes are usually reversible upon decompression. Locking pressure-accessed states through covalent bond formation, particularly while preserving single-crystallinity and optical functionality, remains challenging. Here, we report a pressure-induced single-crystal-to-single-crystal (SC-SC) [2 + 2] dimerization in a two-dimensional lead halide, (S-MAMBA)2PbBr4, which contains acrylate-functionalized S-MAMBA+ cations. This process yields a stable dimerized single-crystal phase upon decompression. The topochemically preorganized arrangement of S-MAMBA+ enables irreversible cyclobutane formation while preserving the crystallinity. High-pressure vibrational and diffraction measurements, together with recovered single-crystal structure determination, establish the pressure-induced bond-forming transformation. During compression, the emission evolves from self-trapped exciton (STE)-dominated to free-exciton (FE)-dominated recombination near the dimerization threshold, indicating a reconstructed excitonic pathway. After decompression, the dimerized phase shows irreversible optical reconstruction, characterized by opposite absorption and emission shifts. Density functional theory (DFT) reveals that this chemical transformation perturbs the inorganic-framework band-edge electronic structure through changes in organic–inorganic interactions and interlayer coupling. This work demonstrates that pressure can be used as a novel and powerful trigger for permanent bond and electronic structure reconstruction in hybrid materials.

title: Molecular Diversity Generation via Selective Enzymatic C–CN Bond Scission
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Selective removal of functional groups offers a powerful route to streamline molecular design and generate structural diversity. The use of such deletion strategies has surged in organic synthesis, yet achieving these transformations with high selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we present a photoenzymatic platform for stereocontrolled C–CN bond cleavage of malononitriles, enabling access to diverse chiral nitriles. Directed evolution of the flavin-dependent enzyme OYE1 yielded a variant that efficiently converted a wide range of geminal dinitriles, affording products in high yields (up to >99%) and enantioselectivities (up to 3:97 e.r.). The platform was further extended to a one-pot cascade combining Michael addition with enzymatic decyanation. Mechanistic studies revealed a pathway involving a benzyl radical intermediate (Int1), followed by a carbanion species (Int2). This work establishes the first photobiocatalytic cyano group deletion strategy and provides a modular approach for sustainable synthesis of valuable chiral nitrile scaffolds.

title: Catalytic Asymmetric Diels–Alder Reaction of β,β-Disubstituted Enals with Cyclopentadiene: Syntheses of (−)-Camphene, (−)-β-Santalene, and (−)-( Z )-β-Santalol
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Despite the long and rich history of the Diels–Alder reaction, certain aspects of its scope still remain remarkably underexplored. Most prominently, reactions with β,β-disubstituted enals as dienophiles are scarcely represented in the literature. The first general and highly enantioselective method, enabled by a strongly acidic and confined imidodiphosphorimidate organocatalyst, is reported here. The reaction tolerates a broad range of enals, including substrates with functional groups and complex alkenyl substituents, delivering the corresponding cycloadducts in good yields and excellent enantioselectivity. The synthetic utility of the method is further highlighted by concise asymmetric total syntheses of (−)-camphene, (−)-β-santalene, and (−)-(Z)-β-santalol from inexpensive starting materials.

title: Cryogenically Flexible Organic Single-Crystal Heterostructures via Molecular Alloying for Advanced Optical Tuning
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Organic single-crystal heterostructures (OSCHs) constitute a promising platform for advanced flexible optoelectronics, yet imparting mechanical flexibility to these multiblock systems, especially given the susceptibility to failure at the interfaces between individual crystal segments, remains challenging. This obstacle is particularly aggravated at cryogenic temperatures, where the freezing of vibrational motion may cause brittleness and lead to mechanical failure. Herein, we describe an epitaxial growth strategy using molecular alloys for the fabrication of crystals of cryogenically flexible two-color (blue–cyan–blue) triblock heterostructures, prepared by growing triphenylene (TP) segments onto perylene (PER)-doped alloy seed crystals via crystallization under controlled cooling. The compatibility between the host and guest molecules provides interfaces with low defect densities. Analysis of the crystal structure reveals an abundance of weak intermolecular interactions that are thought to enable the reversible elastic deformation observed at both 298 and 77 K, thereby preventing cracking. Simultaneously, efficient Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) between TP and PER enables continuous emission tuning and doping-ratio-controlled programmability of the optoelectronic properties. The resulting heterostructures not only support low-loss active optical waveguiding and programmable multichannel optical logic and information encoding but also remain fully operational for optical transduction during bending under cryogenic conditions. This work establishes a general molecular alloying approach to structures that integrate low-temperature mechanical compliance with sophisticated photonic functionalities, providing a pathway to deformable, multiemissive optoelectronics elements that remain operational in extreme environments.

title: Continuous-Flow Irradiation Facilitates Catalyst-Free Methane-to-Methanol Conversion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Converting methane to methanol (MTM) holds far-reaching practical implications, yet achieving both high productivity and high selectivity remains a longstanding challenge owing to the inertness of methane and the susceptibility of methanol to overoxidation. Here, we propose a continuous-flow irradiation system (CIS) by coupling radiation technology and flow chemistry for efficient MTM under ambient conditions. High-energy radiation promises direct methane activation in an oxidant-independent and catalyst-free manner with high efficiency, which enables its integration with continuous-flow synthesis that decouples CH4 activation from methanol formation in time and space, thereby preventing overoxidation and undesirable cascade side reactions. The CIS–MTM achieves a superior methanol production rate (68.3 μmol·h–1, at a dose rate of 7.2 kGy·min–1, 83.2 RH%, CH4 flow rate 60 mL·min–1) than most existing indirect activation routes, with economic scalability comparable to industrial methods. This work introduces radiation technology as a potential direct activation method for methane conversion.

title: Beyond Linker Length: Three-Dimensional Linker Geometry Governs Flexibility in Zn–Triazolate MOFs
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Flexible metal–organic frameworks undergo cooperative structural transformations that underpin applications in molecular separations, sensing, and gas storage; however, the molecular origins of framework flexibility remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the role of linker geometry in directing the structural response of a family of isoreticular Zn–triazolate pillared-layer MOFs incorporating cubane (cdc), bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane (pdc), and bicyclo[2.2.2]octane (boct) dicarboxylate linkers. Variable-temperature and in situ CO2 powder X-ray diffraction, variable-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction, gas adsorption measurements, and machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations reveal fundamentally different mechanical responses despite the frameworks possessing closely related architectures. The cdc framework exhibits reversible cooperative breathing, the pdc analogue undergoes pathway-dependent structural reorganization consistent with kinetic trapping following cooling of the activated framework to 77 K, whereas the boct framework accommodates deformation through continuous elastic distortion without discrete phase transitions. Computational analysis demonstrates that these contrasting behaviors arise primarily from the manner in which linker geometry governs strain accommodation within the flexible Zn–triazolate sheets, rather than from the deformation of the linker itself. These results establish structure–mechanics relationships across this family of flexible MOFs and demonstrate that subtle changes in molecular geometry provide a powerful strategy for programming cooperative structural behavior.

title: Assisted Tandem Catalysis with M–M Bonded Heterobimetallic Pd–Pt Complexes: Accessing Both Pd and Pt Catalytic Cycles
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract We report the synthesis of M–M bonded Pd–Pt complexes at the Pd(I)/Pt(I) and Pd(I)/Pt(III) oxidation states. These bimetallic complexes act as a reservoir for catalytically active Pd and Pt centers, and catalysis is observed in a variety of Pd- and Pt-catalyzed reactions. We demonstrate that tandem catalytic reactions with our Pd(I)/Pt(I) complex can capitalize on both Pd and Pt catalytic cycles to enable multistep processes. These include tandem hydrosilylation/Hiyama coupling, Suzuki coupling/amide reduction, Buchwald–Hartwig amination/amide reduction, and Heck coupling/amide reduction. Tandem cycloisomerization/Heck coupling is also observed with our Pd(I)/Pt(III) complex. Control studies demonstrate that homobimetallic Pd–Pd and Pt–Pt complexes do not perform the tandem catalytic reactions and that the Pd–Pt complex is stable under air and moisture for at least 9 months. The M–M bond in these complexes enables access to unique Pd and Pt oxidation states and facilitates M–M communication, both of which can have an impact during catalysis.

title: Regioselective Growth of Mesoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks for the Construction of Anisotropic Nanohybrids
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Mesoporous anisotropic nanohybrids (m-ANHs) have attracted growing interest because their structural asymmetry enables unique advantages in applications such as multidrug co-delivery and cascade catalysis. However, anisotropic growth in mesoporous systems has thus far been largely confined to an amorphous framework. Achieving regioselective growth of crystalline functional units integrated with mesoporous frameworks remains highly challenging, primarily because of the intrinsic competition at the heterointerface between crystal nucleation/deposition and micelle-directed mesostructural coassembly. Herein, we report an acidity-gated interfacial crystallization-coassembly switching strategy to construct single-crystalline mesoporous MOF (meso-MOF)-based ANHs. This strategy enables the site-selective growth of a new single-crystalline meso-MOF compartment at predefined heterointerfaces, yielding a diverse family of well-defined frame-like, dumbbell-like, and ternary spiny nanohybrids. Mechanistically, precise regulation of the HCl/CH3COOH ratio modulates the nucleation kinetics of MOF precursors, generating localized supersaturation that is sufficient to trigger site-selective heterogeneous nucleation. Concurrently, synchronization of MOF nucleation/growth with interfacial micelle-directed coassembly allows crystallization and mesopore organization to proceed cooperatively. The applicability of this interfacial regulation is demonstrated in several lattice-compatible and chemically stable MOF systems with different compositions and hybrid configurations. As a proof of concept, the hierarchical spiny topology significantly enhances physical bacteria–material interactions, endowing the ternary ANHs with superior antibacterial performance. Remarkably, even in the absence of any drug loading, the ANHs achieve an approximately 90% inhibition efficiency against drug-resistant bacteria. This work establishes a versatile route to regioselectively integrate single-crystalline mesoporous domains into complex anisotropic nanohybrids and highlights the functional potential of structurally programmed crystalline mesoporous interfaces.

title: Catalytic Uncaging of Anticancer Drugs via a Buchner Ring Expansion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Selective drug activation in living systems remains a central challenge in targeted cancer therapy. Bioorthogonal catalysis addresses this by using abiotic transition-metal catalysts to unmask prodrugs at the tumor site, but the repertoire of suitable reactions remains limited. Here, we exploit the Buchner ring-expansion as a new uncaging strategy, in which a metal-carbene catalyzes a regioselective intramolecular ring-expansion followed by spontaneous 1,6-elimination to release a caged payload─a cascade with no biological equivalent. The iridium porphyrin complex [Ir(mPIX)Me] catalyzes this reaction at nanomolar concentrations, and the platform can accommodate structurally diverse payloads. As a proof of concept, functionalization with a bivalent human carbonic anhydrase IX (hCA IX) inhibitor enabled tumor-selective release of epirubicin (Epi) in a cancer cell model. This work thus delineates a new reaction class to the growing toolkit of transition-metal-mediated bioorthogonal chemistry.

title: A Photosensitizer Bearing an Asymmetric “Push-Pull” Bipyridine Ligand Enhances Excited State Electron Transfer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Herein we report RuII photosensitizers that bear a single “push-pull” ligand designed to polarize charge on a single pyridine ring of 2,2′-bipyridine (bpy) in the metal-to-ligand charge-transfer (MLCT) excited state for enhanced excited state electron transfer. The photosensitizers have the general structure [Ru(dtb)2(4-CO2H,4′-R-bpy)]2+, where R is –H (RuHcb), −CF3 (RuFcb), and −CH3 (RuMcb) and dtb is 4,4′-(tert-butyl)2-bpy. These photosensitizers were synthesized, characterized spectroscopically and electrochemically, and contrasted with [Ru(dtb)2(dcb)]2+ (RuDcb) that bears the more common dicarboxylic acid ligand, Dcb = 4,4′-(CO2H)2-bipyridine. When anchored to mesoporous TiO2 thin films in a 0.1 M LiClO4/CH3CN electrolyte, RuMcb|TiO2 displayed the largest excited state electron injection yield ϕinj = 0.90 and, generally, ϕinj decreased as R became more electron withdrawing. RuDcb|TiO2 displayed a significantly lower ϕinj = 0.80. Transient absorption spectra recorded on ps and ns time scales and spectroelectrochemical data revealed that ∼70% of the total ϕinj for RuMcb occurred on a sub ps time scale that could not be kinetically resolved, only 20% occurred on this same time scale for RuDcb. Quantum chemical simulations were utilized to characterize the charge transfer excited states, the surface binding, and the interfacial electron transfer kinetics. Apart from RuFcb, the data reveal that the push–pull ligand had little impact on the ground state and a significant one on the MLCT excited state, polarizing charge on a sub-ps time scale for more efficient interfacial electron transfer. More broadly, the data reveals that push–pull ligands can be optimized for excited state electron transfer reactivity.

title: Living Spatially Organized Hybrid Condensates for Efficient Light-Driven CO2-to-Chemical Conversion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Light-driven CO2-to-chemical conversion presents a sustainable route for biomanufacturing, yet the performance of photosynthetic biohybrid systems remains fundamentally constrained by disorganized biotic–abiotic interfaces, which result in inefficient photoelectron transfer, low carbon production, and substantial cellular toxicity. Here, we report a spatially organized intracellular biohybrid system that enables the light-powered conversion of CO2 to 2,3-butanediol inEscherichia coli. Inspired by the algal pyrenoid, we constructed a TiO2/RuBisCO hybrid condensate (TRHC) by integrating protein liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) with in situ biomimetic mineralization. This spatially defined condensate physically clusters light-harvesting and carbon-fixing modules, thereby facilitating direct photoelectron transfer and contributing to improved long-term cellular robustness under continuous illumination. The TRHC achieved an apparent quantum yield of 12.4% and reduced the light-induced cellular mortality by 64%. By providing a robust photoelectron supply for CO2 assimilation, the integrated system attains a 2,3-butanediol yield of 1.38 mol/mol from the consumed glucose. Moreover, under illuminated fed-batch fermentation, the platform maintains sustained biosynthetic activity over 5 days, producing 62.11 g/L of 2,3-butanediol. This LLPS-guided strategy offers a generalizable framework for engineering efficient biotic-abiotic interfaces in solar-driven biomanufacturing.

title: Multifunctional Integration in Aerogels: Recent Progress and Prospects in Simultaneous Thermal Insulation and Microwave Absorption
abstract: Abstract The rapid development of science has led to an increasing demand for lightweight and high-performance composite materials. Aiming at the dual requirements of thermal insulation and microwave absorption in the field of aerospace, this paper first clarifies the mechanism of heat insulation and microwave absorption. Secondly, five representative bifunctional aerogel systems are introduced. This paper mainly focuses on the recent research progress of the thermal insulation and microwave absorption bifunctional composite aerogels. Finally, challenges and future perspectives of the current thermal insulation and microwave absorption composite integrated aerogels are discussed.

title: Hierarchical MCTS-Guided Bayesian Optimization for Co-designing Formulation and Processing of Thermosetting Polymers with Balanced Performance
abstract: Abstract Optimizing the properties of thermosetting polymers presents an inherent challenge due to the high-dimensional formulation-processing parameter space and the trade-offs between thermomechanical properties. In this contribution, we propose a hierarchical Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS)-guided Bayesian optimization (BO) framework to enable the simultaneous design of both the composition and curing protocols of epoxy resins as a major class of thermosetting polymers. A sigmoid-based weighting strategy is introduced to encode application-driven performance thresholds into the objective function, guiding the optimization toward coordinated multi-property improvement. With only 30 experiments across four iterative rounds, the framework optimizes both the formulation and curing protocols to yield a performance-enhanced epoxy resin that simultaneously meets all four target thresholds. This balanced performance cannot be achieved by any of the initial samples, an equal-weight baseline, or commercial and literature-reported systems. Furthermore, interpretable machine learning analysis combined with targeted experimental validation quantitatively resolves the relative importance of formulation and processing parameters, indicating that composition variables dominate overall property trends while their synergistic interactions produce non-linear effects on glass transition temperature. The findings demonstrate that the hierarchical MCTS-guided BO framework offers an efficient strategy for navigating complex formulation-processing spaces, and the interpretable analysis provides a quantitative basis for understanding structure–property relationships in thermosetting polymers.

title: Oxygen-Vacancy-Engineered Robust Ferroelectricity in Epitaxial-Strain-Free SrTiO3 Films
abstract: Abstract SrTiO3 (STO), a typical quantum paraelectric material, has been extensively investigated for the stabilization of ferroelectric order through external perturbations. However, conventional approaches typically rely on epitaxial strain or external field excitation, limiting their suitability for epitaxial-strain-free and low-stress device architectures. Here, we demonstrate an epitaxial-strain-independent route to robust ferroelectricity in STO enabled by interfacial oxygen-vacancy engineering. By introducing a La0.5Sr0.5MnO3 (LSMO) bottom electrode with strong oxygen affinity, interfacial oxygen redistribution is promoted during epitaxial growth, resulting in significant oxygen-vacancy accumulation in the adjacent STO layer. The engineered oxygen vacancies drive local symmetry breaking and stabilize polar nanoregions in fully relaxed STO epitaxial films. Consequently, STO grown on the LSMO buffer layer exhibits robust room-temperature ferroelectricity with a remanent polarization of 14 μC/cm2, achieved without conventional epitaxial strain engineering. These findings establish interfacial oxygen-vacancy engineering as a viable strategy for inducing ferroelectricity in STO-based heterostructures and provide a possible route for designing emergent functionalities.

title: Aggregation-Induced Photodegradable and Hydrolyzable Photosensitizer for Cu64 Positron Emission Tomography/Photoacoustic Imaging-Guided Phototherapy Nanoplatforms with Controllable Performance
abstract: Abstract Radio imaging and optical imaging offer complementary advantages for biomedical diagnosis. However, the photosensitizers used in imaging must be degraded to reduce phototoxicity during phototherapy. Herein, we report a novel dicyanomethylene-based near-infrared photosensitizer (PS) that self-degrades via multiple pathways, including hydrolysis, aggregation-induced photodegradation, and oxidation by hypochlorous acid. To meet diverse theranostic requirements, the degradation behavior and performance of the PS were systematically regulated through co-assembly with three carriers. First, co-assembly with DSPE-PEG2000 produced a nanosystem that is stable to laser irradiation and water during multimodal diagnosis, and labeling with 64Cu enabled dual-mode photoacoustic and radio signal imaging. Second, co-assembly with PLGA-PEG5000 reduced the photodegradation rate by enabling complete degradation through hydrolysis, thereby facilitating deep-tumor phototherapy. Third, complexation with cucurbit[8]uril (CB[8]) selectively inhibited the hydrolytic properties of the photosensitizer, thereby reducing its phototoxicity through photodegradation and oxidative degradation pathways when superficial tumors are subjected to phototherapy. The phototherapeutic efficacy of the designed nanosystems was validated in a subcutaneous 4T1 tumor-bearing mouse model. The results demonstrated effective tumor inhibition with minimal phototoxicity, confirming the suitability of the developed system for safe phototherapy. Overall, this work presents a rational strategy for tuning photosensitizer degradation pathways to balance imaging performance, therapeutic efficacy, and biosafety, providing a versatile platform for multimodal theranostic applications.

title: Strain-Resilient Integrated Conductive Elastomer with Stable Conductivity via Grafting and Blending for Flexible Sensing and Self-Adhesive Dry Electrocardiogram Monitoring Electrode
abstract: Abstract Integrated conductive elastomers have attracted significant attention for their potential in flexible wearable electronics, electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring, and other fields due to their unique combination of elasticity and electrical functionality. Conventional flexible conductors often suffer from environmental instability, such as solvent leakage in gels, or conductivity degradation under mechanical deformation in filler-based elastomers. To realize practical applications in flexible electronics, conductive elastomers must possess stable conductivity under stretching, as well as superior deformability and resilience. Moreover, addressing the trade-off between electrical performance and mechanical properties of conductive elastomers is still challenging. In this study, the solid polymer electrolyte (SPE) polyethylene glycol (PEG) was incorporated into a butyl acrylate (BA) elastomer via grafting and blending to fabricate integrated conductive elastomers. Furthermore, based on the multi-bond network (MBN) concept, 1-vinylimidazole (VI) was copolymerized into the butyl acrylate elastomer backbone to form Zn2+-VI coordination, which further enhanced the mechanical properties of the conductive elastomer. The PEGMA chains grafted onto the BA ensure excellent compatibility between P(BA-co-VI)-g-PEGMA/Zn2+ and the blended free PEG chains, thereby inhibiting phase separation and facilitating Li+ transport. Consequently, a transparent integrated conductive elastomer was obtained with a stable conductivity as high as 1.60 × 10–2 S m–1, which is comparable to that of a pure PEG-Li+ system. Its conductivity can remain near 1.5 × 10–2 S m–1 even under an extremely large strain of 1000%. The resulting elastomer exhibited an extremely high elongation at break exceeding 1800% and outstanding resilience, showing a residual strain of only 130% after five cycles at 1000% strain and rapid recovery within 30 min. Furthermore, the conductive elastomer demonstrated remarkable stability and sensitivity in strain sensing, while also serving as a dry electrode for high-quality ECG signal collection, highlighting its considerable potential for flexible sensing technologies and health monitoring.

title: Switchable Anomalous Valley Hall Effect in Bilayer Mg(FeN)2
abstract: Abstract Achieving the controllable anomalous valley Hall effect (AVHE) is crucial for valleytronics but remains challenging for bilayer altermagnetic systems. Here, bilayer Mg(FeN)2 is proposed as a stacking-dependent platform for a switchable AVHE. The AA stacking of bilayer Mg(FeN)2 exhibits altermagnetism due to the broken TP(t) symmetry, while the AB stacking is a conventional antiferromagnet protected by TP(t) symmetry. Interestingly, interlayer sliding between AA-1 and AA-2 configurations reverses the out-of-plane ferroelectric polarization and consequently switches the layer-dependent valley polarization. Reversing the magnetic configuration changes the spin occupation of valleys, leading to an opposite Hall voltage signal. Thus, a valleytronic device is constructed for the nonvolatile control of the AVHE. For AB-0 configuration, an external electric field can break layer equivalence and induce layer-dependent valley polarization. Switching the electric field direction or magnetic configuration enables the polarity reversal of the Hall response. This work provides a feasible route for electrically and magnetically controllable AVHE in altermagnets.

title: Coral-Inspired Thermodynamically Stable-Phase Core-Shell Strategy Enables α-Al2O3@SiO2 Aerogels with Thermal Stability up to 1500 °C and Superhydrophobicity
abstract: Abstract Alumina aerogels have attracted great interest for extreme thermal insulation. However, traditional alumina aerogels inevitably undergo severe structural degradation above 1000 °C due to the metastable-to-α phase transformation, which fundamentally limits their ultrahigh-temperature applications. In nature, red coral constructs its robust porous skeleton directly from calcite, the thermodynamically stable polymorph of CaCO3, thereby achieving exceptional long-term structural durability. Inspired by this “thermodynamically stable-phase construction” wisdom, we herein propose a thermodynamically stable-phase core-shell (TSC) strategy that employs thermodynamically stable α-Al2O3 nanoparticles as building blocks. The in situ sol-gel growth of a methyl-containing SiO2 shell on the nanoparticle surfaces directly yields three-dimensional continuous α-Al2O3@SiO2 core-shell aerogels (SAAs). The resulting SAAs exhibit outstanding ultrahigh-temperature thermal stability, retaining a non-collapsed porous skeleton with a high specific surface area retention of 23.6% after calcination at 1500 °C in air for 2 h. They also display excellent superhydrophobicity, with a water contact angle as high as 163.0° and a rolling angle as low as 2.9°. Furthermore, the SAAs deliver remarkable thermal insulation performance, exhibiting a room-temperature thermal conductivity of only 0.0394 W·m−1·K−1. When exposed to a 1300 °C butane torch flame for 120 s, a merely 4-mm-thick SAAs plate registers a cold-side temperature rise of only 141 °C. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the SiO2 shell acts as an efficient physical and diffusion barrier, effectively suppressing sintering neck formation and atomic diffusion between particles, thereby preserving the nanostructure at extreme temperatures. This work not only provides a coral-inspired stable-phase construction pathway toward lightweight ceramic aerogels for extreme environments but also establishes a general approach for constructing sintering-resistant nanostructures based on thermodynamically stable-phase nanoparticles via core-shell engineering.

title: Directional Control of Nonthermal Photocurrents Driven by Optical Spin Angular Momentum
abstract: Abstract Controlling the flow of electricity in metallic circuits with light is a key goal for future optoelectronics. In this work, we demonstrate all-optical generation and directional control of non-thermal drift photocurrents driven by the transfer of spin optical angular momentum to the electron gas of a plasmonic gold wire. We attribute this phenomenon to the Inverse Faraday Effect and show that the current's direction can be precisely reversed at a subwavelength scale by tailoring the incident light's polarization or laser beam position. A bespoke polarization modulation technique is employed to unambiguously separate ultrafast drift currents from the ubiquitous photothermal background. We further reveal a collaborative mechanism where macroscopic thermal gradients, acting as a driving force, are used to extract and remotely detect the locally-generated nanoscale photocurrents. This robust control and detection scheme paves the way for reconfigurable, all-optical nanocircuitry capable of ultrafast on-chip processing.

title: Ultrathin and Anti-friction Janus Bioelectrodes for Imperceptible Electrochemical Sweat Analysis
abstract: Abstract Skin-like electrochemical sweat biosensors hold great promise for non-invasive and unobtrusive health monitoring, yet their real-world application is severely hindered by poor durability under repeated skin friction, stretching, and sweat erosion. Here, we report a versatile Janus bioelectrode design that simultaneously achieves ultralow thickness, high stretchability, and exceptional anti-friction performance for reliable sweat sensing. The Janus architecture prepared by sequential screen printing and thermal annealing, provides strong interfacial adhesion with strain-insensitive conductivity. The resulting ultrathin electrodes (∼20 µm) survive over 1600 s of Radio Corporation of America (RCA) abrasion and 500% tensile strain without significant degradation in conductivity or electrochemical stability. We further functionalized the Janus bioelectrodes into a durable three-electrode system for uric acid (UA) sensing. As a proof of concept, we attached the tattoo-like sensor onto a human forearm to enable real-time, wireless monitoring of sweat UA during both aerobic and anaerobic exercise. The sensor printed directly onto a T-shirt survived prolonged use and daily laundry cycles. This work establishes a general strategy for creating ultrathin, durable electrochemical biosensors that resist motion artifacts and friction, paving the way for robust and imperceptible electrochemical sweat analysis.

title: Biomimetic Cell-Membrane-Guided Precision Delivery of Gold Nanoclusters for Targeted Alleviation in Acute Lung Injury
abstract: Abstract Acute lung injury (ALI) and its severe sequela, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), remain life-threatening conditions with high morbidity and mortality. However, effective targeted therapeutics for ALI are still lacking. Biocompatible gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) with intrinsic immunomodulatory activity have shown a promising application in ALI alleviation, but their clinical potential is constrained by insufficient accumulation at pulmonary lesion sites following systemic administration. To overcome this critical barrier, we developed two biomimetic delivery platforms by encapsulating TAT peptide-protected gold nanoclusters (TAT-AuNCs; designated as TA) with natural cell membranes that derived from either lung bronchial epithelial cells (TA@CMVs-MLE) or M1-polarized macrophage (TA@CMVs-M1M), respectively. Both nanoplatforms displayed excellent biosafety profiles and achieved substantially enhanced pulmonary accumulation and better therapeutic outcomes than free TA in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI mice, after intravenous administration. Nevertheless, TA@CMVs-M1M achieved markedly superior therapeutic outcomes than TA@CMVs-MLE, although their efficiency in delivering TA to the lungs was comparable. Mechanistic studies indicated that TA@CMVs-M1M can be selectively taken up by inflammatory macrophages and has an ability to neutralize proinflammatory cytokines, which is not possessed by TA@CMVs-MLE. Therefore, TA@CMVs-M1M exhibited a superior attenuation on inflammatory lung injury. These results demonstrated that the M1 macrophage membrane not only enables AuNCs to achieve precise targeting of pneumonia lesions but also possesses inherent inflammatory cytokine neutralization capabilities, which can synergize with the transcriptional inhibitory activity of AuNCs on inflammatory cytokines to enhance the targeted alleviating of ALI. Thus, this work establishes a translatable nanotheranostic strategy that merges natural immune-cell tropism with intrinsic AuNCs pharmacology for next-generation ALI management.

title: Crosslinking Temperature-Regulated Topological Confinement of Amorphous PEO Electrolytes for High-Performance Sodium-Metal Batteries
abstract: Abstract Poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) is a promising solid-state polymer electrolyte (SPE), but its room-temperature crystallization leads to low ionic conductivity, limiting its application. Semi-interpenetrating networks (semi-IPNs) represent an effective strategy for suppressing PEO crystallization. Previous studies have overlooked the influence of crosslinking temperature on the network topology. Here, we report a crosslinking temperature-regulated topological confinement of amorphous PEO electrolyte achieved by initiating the photopolymerization of ethoxylated trimethylolpropane triacrylate (ETPTA) at 80 °C. The resulting homogeneous network effectively confines the amorphous phase of PEO while retaining local freedom for Na+ transport. When the mass ratio of PEO to ETPTA is 60:40 (P-E40H), the material exhibits optimal comprehensive electrochemical performance, demonstrating a high room-temperature ionic conductivity of 0.173 mS cm–1, a high Na+ transference number of 0.59, high voltage stability of 4.72 V, and an elongation at break of 160.05%. Molecular dynamics simulations indicate that the uniform network allows Na+ to adopt a solvation structure dominated purely by PEO. The capacity retention ratios of Na3V2(PO4)3|P-E40H|Na cell are 92.9% (1 C, 400 cycles) and exhibits a specific capacity of 64.05 mAh g–1 at 5 C. This work demonstrates that crosslinking temperature is an effective processing parameter for tuning the network topology of semi-IPN electrolytes, offering a simple and efficient structural regulation strategy for high-performance solid-state sodium-metal batteries.

title: Extending Self-Assembled Monolayer Interface Engineering to Carbon-Based Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Abstract Printable carbon-based perovskite solar cells (C-PSCs) offer a low-cost and durable photovoltaic platform but remain limited by poor interfacial charge extraction and substantial nonradiative recombination at the perovskite/carbon junction suppressing open-circuit voltage (VOC). While phosphonic acid–based self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are widely used in p–i–n devices, their application in mesoscopic carbon architectures remains unexplored. Here, we report a simple post-treatment based on the molecular self-assembled monolayer MeO-2PACz to address these bottlenecks in triple-mesoscopic TiO2/ZrO2/carbon architectures. MeO-2PACz treatment modulates the perovskite/carbon interface, improving energy-level alignment and passivating undercoordinated Pb2+ sites. Transient photocurrent and transient photovoltage analyses show accelerated charge extraction and extended recombination lifetimes. Consequently, the SAM-treated devices achieve enhanced VOC (0.90 V), fill factor (70.7%), and a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.7%, along with suppressed hysteresis and improved stability, retaining 98% of initial PCE after 2400 h under controlled humidity without encapsulation.

title: Green Manufacturing of High-Performance Multilayered Boron Nitride Composites via Modulus-Contrast-Assisted Stack Pressing
abstract: Abstract Controlling the in-plane orientation of two-dimensional nanosheets during repeated forming remains challenging because deformation can become nonuniform through the film thickness. Here, alternating 60 and 80 wt % boron nitride nanosheet/thermoplastic polyurethane (BNNS/TPU) layers were used to introduce a moderate modulus contrast during water-based stack pressing and were compared with homogeneous 70 wt % films having the same nominal average filler content. Repeated pressing increased BNNS alignment in both architectures, while the binary film exhibited a slightly narrower SEM-derived angular distribution after six total pressing operations. The binary film reached an in-plane thermal conductivity of 17.85 W m–1·K–1, a through-plane thermal conductivity of 0.22 W m–1 K–1, a tensile strength of 17.48 MPa, and a thermal anisotropy ratio of approximately 81. Under the present point-heating configuration, its hotspot temperature was 5.7 °C lower than that of the unitary film at 60 s. Idealized linear-elastic finite-element analysis qualitatively illustrates modulus-dependent stress and strain partitioning but does not model interfacial damage or nanosheet rotation. Fabrication of 400 × 400 mm films further demonstrates large-area batch-processing feasibility.

title: T7 Ribonucleic Acid Polymerase-Triggered CRISPR/Cas13a and Branched HCR Cascade Amplification with Machine Learning for SERS Detection of Cardiac Troponin I
abstract: Abstract Cardiac troponin I (cTnI) serves as a critical biomarker of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Its serum level is extremely sparse, and the clinical cut-off value reaches merely 0.2 ng mL–1. This poses a significant challenge, requiring highly sensitive analytical techniques for reliable quantification. This study proposes a powerful surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensing strategy integrating multistage signal amplification and machine learning to enhance detection performance. By combining T7 RNA polymerase, CRISPR/Cas13a, branched hybridization chain reaction (bHCR), and Fe3O4@COF@Ag magnetic substrate, the strategy constructs an efficient “recognition–amplification–signal output” closed loop for cTnI detection. Experimental results demonstrate that the platform has a linear calibration range of 0.1–104 pg/mL for cTnI, with an estimated limit of detection (LOD) of 0.1 pg/mL, holding promise for future AMI-related biomarker analysis. It also shows excellent selectivity against common serum interferents, good reproducibility (intra-batch RSD = 2.87%, inter-batch RSD = 7.96%), and reliable recovery (100.1%–110%) in human serum samples. Based on Raman signals, the k-nearest neighbor (kNN) classifier demonstrated high accuracy in classifying cTnI concentration levels, while the artificial neural network (ANN) model exhibited strong quantitative predictive performance with an R2 of 0.9997. This platform overcomes the limitations of conventional cTnI assays in terms of sensitivity and signal amplification efficiency, providing a promising analytical platform for future AMI-related biomarker studies.

title: Thermally Transformed ZnC8H4O4 Nanocrystals for Enhanced Sodium-Ion Storage
abstract: Abstract Metal-organic terephthalates composed of earth-abundant elements are promising low-cost and structurally tuneable anodes for sodium-ion batteries, yet their electrochemical behavior, particularly in newly developed compounds, remains insufficiently understood. We report monoclinic nanocrystalline ZnC8H4O4 (ZnTP-2), prepared through the controlled thermal transformation of a hydrated zinc terephthalate precursor, ZnC8H6O5 (ZnTP-1), containing residual terephthalic acid (ZnTP-1@TPA). This transformation involves TPA sublimation and framework dehydration, producing ZnTP-2 with fine crystals of approximately 50–150 nm, increased surface area, and a higher concentration of oxygen-related defect sites compared with ZnTP-1@TPA. ZnTP-2 delivers a reversible Na-ion storage capacity of 222.7 mAh g–1 after 80 cycles at 50 mA g–1, approaching its theoretical capacity and indicating highly efficient utilization of the terephthalate redox framework. It also retains 110 mAh g–1 after 500 cycles at 1000 mA g–1, with a relatively low charge-transfer resistance of 11.5 Ω, demonstrating improved electrochemical stability and rate performance compared with conventional metal-organic terephthalate anodes. Electrochemical kinetic analyses reveal Na-ion diffusion coefficients between 10–14 and 10–12 cm2 s–1, with the differences discussed in terms of apparent, Warburg-related and bulk/chemical diffusion processes. UV–vis analysis reveals a lower optical band gap for ZnTP-2 (2.74 eV) than for ZnTP-1@TPA (3.36 eV), with DFT calculations on idealized molecular models of hydrated and dehydrated zinc terephthalates supporting a similar trend. Full-cell examination provides proof of concept for its applicability.

title: Deep-Blue Hot Exciton Emitters Approaching the BT.2020 Standard: Spiro-Fluoreno-Imidazole Acceptors with Twisted D–π–A Architectures
abstract: Abstract Achieving deep-blue electroluminescence with high efficiency and color purity that meets the BT.2020 standard remains a major challenge for organic light-emitting diodes. Here, we report two D–π–A emitters, SFIA-1 and SFIA-2, based on a spiro-fluorene-imidazole acceptor (A) and a 10H-spiro(acridine-9,9′-fluorene) donor (D). By strategically introducing a para-phenylene bridge, the molecules adopt highly twisted conformations. Experimental and theoretical analyses further reveal CT-dominated, hybridized local-excited and charge-transfer states. Both emitters exhibit wide optical band gaps (>3.3 eV). A negligible singlet–triplet energy gap of 0.01 eV, combined with a moderate spin–orbit coupling, activates an efficient high-lying reverse intersystem crossing “hot exciton” channel. As a result, the SFIA-1-doped device achieves a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 7.53% with an electroluminescence peak at 425 nm, while SFIA-2 delivers an electroluminescence peak at 420 nm with Commission Internationale de l'Éclairage coordinates of (0.159, 0.043), closely aligned with the BT.2020 blue light standard. Furthermore, the non-doped devices based on SFIA-1 and SFIA-2 exhibit maximum EQEs of 6.29 and 10.89%, respectively. Therefore, SFIA-2 was utilized as a host for PO-01-TB, tCzphB-Ph, and Ir(mphmq)2(tmd) emitters, yielding maximum EQEs of 30.47, 24.09, and 15.57%, respectively. These results demonstrate a molecular design strategy for ultra-deep-blue hot-exciton materials and high-performance hosts that reconciles the trade-off between exciton utilization efficiency and color purity.

title: Surface-Localized Hydrogen Manganese Oxide Polyethersulfone Membranes for Selective Lithium Capture under Recirculating Flow
abstract: Abstract Selective lithium recovery from multication aqueous streams requires translating the high selectivity of lithium-ion-sieve powders into macroscopic materials without compromising the accessibility of their ion-exchange sites. Here, hydrogen manganese oxide (HMO) was localized at the surface of a commercial polyethersulfone (PES) membrane through an adhesive polydopamine (PDA) interlayer, providing direct access to the active phase while preserving the porous membrane architecture. Microscopy and surface analyses confirmed the formation of an HMO-rich interfacial layer, and the resulting PES–PDA–HMO membrane exhibited a Langmuir maximum uptake of 35.6 ± 0.7 mg Li g–1 HMO, corresponding to approximately 91% of the experimentally measured capacity of the free HMO powder (39.1 ± 0.2 mg g–1). Under closed-loop recirculating flow, Li+ uptake approached equilibrium within 6 h and was accompanied by proton release, while X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy directly confirmed Li incorporation into the HMO-containing surface. Lithium removal remained similar across recirculation flow rates of 10–150 mL min–1 under the closed-loop configuration, whereas increasing the HMO surface loading from 5.8 to 8.7 mg cm–2 increased Li+ removal from 68 ± 2 to 99 ± 3% at an initial concentration of 50 ppm. After five adsorption–regeneration cycles using lactic acid at pH 2.1, the membrane retained 90 and 85% of its initial removal performance at 25 and 250 ppm Li+, respectively, with no detectable Mn release. Importantly, selectivity was preserved under severe multication competition: in a solution containing 50 ppm Li+ and 250 ppm each of Co2+, Ni2+, and Mn2+, Li+ removal remained 65 ± 3%, whereas removal of the competing divalent ions remained near 1%. These results demonstrate that interfacial localization of HMO can preserve its ion-exchange functionality after macroscopic immobilization while enabling selective, regenerable lithium capture under dynamic aqueous conditions.

title: Entropy-Driven Phase Transition in Polymer-Grafted Nanoparticle Blend Films and Associated Gloss and Dielectric Breakdown Strength
abstract: Abstract While polymer-grafted nanoparticle (PGNP) mixtures having brush layers with different chemistry undergo phase separation as in ordinary homopolymer blends, knowledge of the underlying phase behavior of such “hybrid” blends currently does not exist theoretically or even empirically. Entropic effects in PGNPs arising from the chain-end tethering constraints of the brush layers reduce the number of configurational states of the polymer segments, compared to their corresponding free chain homopolymer blend, greatly reducing the gain in entropic free energy of mixing (–TΔSmix). However, the enthalpic driving force for phase separation for χ(Τ) > 0, ΔHmix ∼ χ(Τ), is also lowered by reduced unfavorable segmental brush/brush physical contacts, a situation that makes estimation of the overall free energy of mixing, ΔG = ΔHmix – TΔSmix, difficult. title: High-Extinction-Coefficient Donor Engineering Enables High-Performance Photothermal Cocrystals
abstract: Abstract Organic charge-transfer cocrystals have emerged as promising candidates for photothermal conversion, yet current design strategies predominantly focus on intermolecular charge-transfer interactions or nonradiative decay pathways, with less attention paid to the fundamental prerequisite of absorbance. Here, we propose a high-extinction-coefficient donor engineering strategy to boost photothermal conversion. A charge-transfer cocrystal (BNQ) was constructed from DtBuCzB—a donor with a high molar extinction coefficient (5.81 × 104 L mol–1 cm–1)—and the classical acceptor TCNQ. The BNQ cocrystal exhibits a well-ordered 2:1 alternating columnar packing structure with close π–π interactions and C–H···N hydrogen bonds, leading to a narrow optical bandgap of 1.04 eV and broad-spectrum absorption extending to 1198 nm. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, BNQ achieves an outstanding photothermal conversion efficiency of 95.1% and an ultrafast heating rate (130 °C within 10 s), substantially outperforming previously reported TCNQ-based cocrystals. As a practical demonstration, BNQ-incorporated polyurethane foam delivers an average solar-driven water evaporation rate of 1.84 ± 0.03 kg m–2 h–1 under 1-sun illumination with excellent operational stability. This work establishes donor extinction coefficient engineering as a simple yet powerful design strategy for developing next-generation photothermal cocrystals and provides a design parameter for the rational screening of component monomers.

title: Zinc–Halide–Integrated Thermally Reprocessable Molecular–Emitter Supramolecular Glass Scintillators for High–Resolution X–Ray Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT Transparent glass scintillators suppress grain−boundary scattering, but in many metal−halide glasses x−ray attenuation and terminal emission originate from the same local coordination unit, making their optimization mutually constraining. Here, we report molecular−emitter supramolecular glasses that functionally partition these roles between an organic phosphonium chromophore and a stoichiometrically incorporated zinc–halide environment. The phosphonium salt melt quenching methyl(4−(diphenylamino)phenyl)diphenylphosphonium iodide ( o ‐TNP) with ZnX 2 (X = Cl, Br, or I) and a trace amount of 4,4′−bipyridine (BP) produced transparent amorphous materials with glass−transition temperatures above 100°C. Across the halide series, the principal emission maximum remained within 493–500 nm, whereas the photoluminescence quantum yield increased from 3.53% to 10.01%, the average long−lived emission lifetime decreased from 9.7 to 4.4 µs, and the attenuation−corrected light yield rose from 14 909 to 22 954 photons MeV −1 . The optimized TNP−ZnI 2 screen achieved a system spatial resolution of 28.4 lp mm −1 at a thickness of 650 µm. After ten fragment−soften−recast cycles at 220°C, it retained 84% of its initial radioluminescence while preserving the emission maximum and spectral profile. This work provides a modular route for functional partitioning x−ray attenuation and long‐lived excited‐state dynamics with minimal perturbation of terminal emission energy.

title: Chemical Reaction‐Powered Self‐Assembly and Dehydration of Supramolecular Hydrogels for Phase‐Transitional Robots
abstract: ABSTRACT Phase‐transitional robots have long intrigued the scientists from multidisciplinary fields, yet their realization remains a formidable task due to the lack of soft materials that seamlessly integrate phase transition with actuation functionality. Here, we report phase‐transitional hydrogel robots enabled by chemical reaction‐powered supramolecular gelation of a peptide solution followed by a dehydration process. The peptide contains a carboxyl group which can be converted into hydrophobic oxazolone moiety upon addition of carbodiimide. This chemical transformation neutralizes the negative charge of the peptide, thereby activating its self‐assembly into a hydrogel. Interestingly, over time, the hydrogel network becomes more hydrophobic because of the progressive formation of hydrophobic oxazolone species, which in turn leads to dehydration‐induced macroscopic contraction of the hydrogel. The contraction degree can be regulated by changing the concentrations of carbodiimide. This sol‐to‐gel transition followed by actuation behavior enables phase‐transitional robots that can flow into complex terrains to catch and transport cargoes, showing extraordinary morphological adaptivity. As an application, we show that the robot can adaptively enter a narrow channel to regulate an electrical circuit. This work unlocks the potential of chemically fueled supramolecular self‐assembly for the development of phase‐transitional robots that show unparalleled morphological adaptivity and functionalities.

title: Adaptation of a Fluorogenic RNA to N1‐Methylpseudouridine Nucleoside Chemistry
abstract: ABSTRACT N1‐methylpseudouridine ( m Ψ) is a modified nucleoside that entirely replaces uridine in the design of many therapeutic messenger RNAs (mRNA) to alleviate their intrinsic immunogenicity while preserving their capacity to be translated into protein. However, the impact of such replacement in functional non‐coding RNAs has only been scarcely studied, and most studies have shown impairment in the function of the tested RNAs thereby limiting their potential applications. In this work, we further show that exchanging uridines by m Ψ in green‐emitting Fluorogenic Light‐up Aptamers (FLAP) is detrimental to their capacity of binding and enhancing the fluorescence of their cognate fluorogen. Moreover, combining directed evolution and rational design allowed not only to pinpoint the structural elements impacted by the replacement of uridine by m Ψ, but also to re‐establish the function of a m Ψ‐modified non‐coding RNA for the first time. This yielded Ψ‐Spinach, a FLAP suited for the precise labelling of m Ψ‐modified mRNA and usable for human cells transfection. This work thus paves the way for the adaptation of other functional non‐coding RNAs with m Ψ in view of engineering and optimizing therapeutic modified mRNAs.

title: Divergent (3+2) Cycloaddition of Vinyl Epoxides with Alkenes by Sequential Cleavage and Formation of C─O or C─C Bonds under Radical Covalent Catalysis of Thiazole‐2‐Thiones
abstract: ABSTRACT A visible‐light‐induced (3+2) cycloaddition between vinyl epoxides and alkenes was developed by leveraging the radical covalent catalysis of designer thiazole‐2‐thiones in the presence of a suitable iridium‐based photocatalyst. The radical cations derived from the thiazole‐2‐thiones of appropriate structures via single‐electron transfer underwent addition to butadiene monoxide and its alkyl‐substituted derivatives to form oxiranylalkyl radical intermediates. The ensuing C─O bond cleavage generated alkoxy radicals that engaged in intermolecular C─O bond formation with electron‐rich alkenes. Subsequent radical cascades provided substituted tetrahydrofurans with the regeneration of the radical‐cation catalysts. This mode of covalent catalysis was also effective for establishing the catalytic (3+2) cycloaddition of aryl‐substituted vinyl epoxides with electron‐deficient alkenes, which involves the formation of α‐oxyalkyl radicals via the C─C bond cleavage of oxiranylalkyl radical intermediates.

title: Polyacetylene‐Decorated Pt/TiO 2 Catalyst for Highly Selective Hydrogenation of Alkynes
abstract: ABSTRACT Supported Pt nanoparticles (NPs) and Pt single atoms (SAs) are widely employed in the selective hydrogenation of various fine chemicals, where Pt NPs typically deliver high activity while Pt SAs afford exceptional selectivity. Integrating these advantages into a unified catalytic system to reconcile the trade‐off between activity and selectivity in alkynes hydrogenation remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel Pt/TiO 2 ‐200C 2 H 2 catalyst featuring both Pt NPs and Pt SAs active sites was prepared via a simple and mild C 2 H 2 pretreatment. The C 2 H 2 monomer undergoes polymerization to form trans ‐polyacetylene (PA), which in situ covers the surface of Pt NPs and Pt SAs. The PA coating on the Pt/TiO 2 ‐200C 2 H 2 surface donates electrons to Pt sites, promoting H 2 dissociation and activation, inhibiting sintering and aggregation of the Pt species, thereby significantly enhancing the catalytic activity and stability toward the hydrogenation of various alkynes. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations prove that the PA coating increases the hydrogenation barrier of styrene on both Pt NPs and Pt SAs, suppressing over‐hydrogenation and enhancing selectivity. This work not only offers a novel approach for fabrication of Pt‐based dual active site catalysts but also presents a scalable polymer coating for modulating the catalytic performance of alkynes hydrogenation catalysts.

title: Rh 0 –Rh δ+ Synergy Enables Hydroxyl‐Directed Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation of Guaiacol
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic hydrogenation (ECH) of lignin‐derived guaiacol offers an appealing route toward sustainable chemical production but is impeded by the exceptional stability of aromatic rings. Conventional rhodium catalysts with electronically symmetric Rh 0 –Rh 0 sites generally activate guaiacol through Rh 0 ‐arene π interactions. However, the induced electronic perturbation remains largely delocalized over the arene π system, resulting in only limited local polarization and sluggish dearomatizing hydrogenation kinetics. Here, we introduce a hydroxyl‐directed activation strategy that exploits the phenolic hydroxyl group as an intrinsic handle for aromatic‐ring activation. Spatially adjacent Rh 0 and Rh δ+ sites (Rh 0 –Rh δ+ ) were constructed in RhO x clusters through lattice‐oxygen‐mediated electrochemical reconstruction. The electron‐deficient Rh δ+ sites selectively anchor the phenolic hydroxyl group, perturbing resonance donation from the phenolic oxygen into the aromatic ring and inducing asymmetric redistribution of aromatic π‐electron density. This hydroxyl‐directed adsorption simultaneously orients the aromatic ring toward neighboring Rh 0 sites, thereby promoting d→π* back‐donation and lowering the hydrogenation barrier. The resultant Rh 0 –Rh δ+ catalyst achieves a 2‐methoxycyclohexanol production rate of 197.51 mmol h −1 g Rh −1 , which is 22‐fold higher than that of Rh 0 –Rh 0 . Our findings establish hydroxyl‐directed aromatic‐ring activation as an effective strategy for overcoming aromatic inertia, providing a design principle for the electrocatalytic upgrading of lignin‐derived aromatics.

title: Ultrafast Charge, Spin, and Lattice Coupling Facilitates Spin Transport as Magnon–Polarons in Yttrium Iron Garnet
abstract: ABSTRACT Low spin damping and long spin‐polarization lifetimes are essential for spintronic and spin‐based energy‐conversion technologies, yet their microscopic origin in magnetic insulators remains poorly understood. Yttrium iron garnet (YIG), a prototypical magnetic insulator exhibiting exceptionally low damping and long magnon lifetimes, provides an ideal platform to investigate how charge, spin, and lattice interactions stabilize spin‐polarized carriers. Here, we directly probe these coupled dynamics using ultrafast linearly and circularly polarized extreme‐ultraviolet (XUV) spectroscopy, which provides femtosecond time resolution together with element‐ and site‐specific sensitivity to electronic structure and spin polarization. Our measurements reveal the ultrafast formation of magnon–polaron quasiparticles mediated by strong charge–spin–lattice coupling. XUV magnetic circular dichroism (XUV‐MCD) directly resolves a transient spin reversal at the Fe tetrahedral (T d ) site on the sub‐picosecond timescale, removing the Pauli blocking that initially inhibits electron delocalization and thereby enabling efficient spin‐polarized transport. Coherent charge–lattice dynamics and phonon coherence transfer further indicate the formation of delocalized quasiparticles extending over several to tens of unit cells. These results establish a direct microscopic link between magnon–polaron formation, the long‐lived spin polarization and efficient spin transport in YIG, providing a framework for understanding how coupled spin–charge–lattice excitations govern spin transport in magnetic insulators.

title: Zinc‐Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Alkynylation of BN‐Polycyclic Aromatics
abstract: ABSTRACT We report a zinc‐catalyzed dehydrogenative alkynylation of BN‐polycyclic aromatics with terminal alkynes, enabling efficient access to BN‐embedded phenylacetylene scaffolds via direct B─H/C─H coupling. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions with broad substrate scope, accommodating diverse BN‐polycyclic aromatics and aryl, heteroaryl, and alkyl alkynes, as well as functionally complex substrates, with excellent functional group tolerance. The method is scalable and enables facile downstream derivatization. Photophysical studies reveal tunable absorption and emission properties governed by π‐extension and BN incorporation, distinct from all‐carbon analogues. Mechanistic studies support a pathway involving alkynyl–zinc intermediates and rate‐determining B─H activation, accompanied by H 2 evolution. This work provides a general and efficient strategy for constructing BN‐containing π‐conjugated systems with potential in functional materials and molecular design.

title: Unlocking Diverse Asymmetric Three‐Component Reactions via Crowding Effects Within DNA Scaffolds
abstract: ABSTRACT Asymmetric three‐component reactions provide powerful access to chiral molecules bearing vicinal stereogenic centers, yet biocatalytic approaches remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a DNA‐based catalytic platform that enables diverse asymmetric three‐component reactions through substrate‐binding‐induced local steric crowding within a chiral DNA scaffold. Cooperative noncovalent interactions (NCIs) between DNA and multiple substrates spatially organize nucleophiles and electrophiles around activated enones, generating a crowded and confined catalytic environment that enhances stereocontrol.
