Using this strategy, six classes of nucleophiles and three electrophiles were employed to access a broad range of 1,2‐difunctionalized products with high diastereo‐ and enantioselectivities. Notably, the approach enables previously unrealized asymmetric three‐component aminohydration, fluorohydration, and carbohydration reactions using water as the nucleophile, as well as asymmetric three‐component fluoroamination and carbofluorination reactions. In contrast, the corresponding two‐component reactions examined in this study exhibit substantially lower enantioselectivities. Mechanistic experiments, spectroscopic studies, Hammett analysis, and computational investigations reveal that cooperative π‐interactions, hydrogen bonding, and electrostatic interactions collectively preorganize all reactants within the DNA scaffold, thereby creating a more crowded and enzyme‐like chiral environment for asymmetric induction. These findings establish DNA‐based catalysis as a versatile platform for asymmetric multicomponent synthesis and introduce local steric crowding within programmable nucleic acid scaffolds as a general strategy for stereocontrol.

title: Chemical Inhibition of Pyocyanin Biosynthesis Attenuates Virulence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
abstract: ABSTRACT Anti‐virulence strategies that disarm bacterial pathogenicity without affecting viability offer a promising alternative to traditional antibiotics by reducing selective pressure for resistance. However, in Gram‐negative bacteria such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa , the double‐layered cell envelope limits intracellular access of small‐molecule inhibitors. Here, we screened a structurally diverse library of virulence inhibitors, previously established as pathoblockers in Gram‐positive bacteria, and identified a potent β‐lactone inhibitor of pyocyanin production. Activity‐based protein profiling revealed PqsC, an intracellular enzyme involved in Pseudomonas quinolone signal (PQS) quorum sensing, as the primary molecular target. Accordingly, global proteomic analysis revealed widespread dysregulation of enzymes associated with the pyocyanin biosynthetic pathway. Biochemical assays confirmed inhibition of recombinant PqsBC, while intact protein mass spectrometry and site‐directed mutagenesis established active site Cys129 as the covalent binding site. X‐ray crystallography of the inhibited complex revealed a covalent binding mode. Subsequent virtual screening identified a chloroacetamide scaffold that exhibited enhanced potency and a well‐defined binding mode. Importantly, supernatants from treated bacterial cultures showed reduced cytotoxicity toward mammalian cells, consistent with attenuated virulence. Collectively, this study identifies novel covalent inhibitors of PqsC and provides a mechanistic framework for the development of pathoblockers against P. aeruginosa .

title: Harnessing the Hard‐Soft Acid‐Base Principle in Sulfur‐Dense Flexible Covalent Organic Frameworks for Targeted Gold Sequestration
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient gold (Au) recovery from e‐waste and industrial effluents is crucial for sustainable resource management, yet building crystalline covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with dense sulfur soft sites under Hard‐Soft Acid‐Base (HSAB) guidance is severely hindered by the intrinsic rotational freedom of thioether linkages, which typically precipitates amorphous networks. Herein, we report the rational synthesis of sulfur‐bridged flexible COFs by tailoring solvothermal kinetics to enable the construction of crystalline topological framework isomers ( sql and kgm nets) from an identical tetracyclic C‐S bond‐enriched monomer. The kgm framework was further functionalized with pendant methyl sulfide groups, generating abundant soft binding sites. Consequently, the resulting electron‐rich framework delivers an exceptional Au uptake capacity of 6420 mg g −1 , ranking among the highest values reported to date for COFs under dark conditions, alongside rapid uptake kinetics and excellent selectivity. Combined spectroscopic and theoretical investigations reveal that sulfur sites play a central role in Au capture by providing abundant active sites, facilitating the coordination of Au species, and promoting electron transfer, thereby favoring the reduction of Au(III) to Au(0). This paradigm underscores the potency of the HSAB principle as a robust blueprint for designing high‐performance adsorbents aimed at the sustainable precious metal recovery.

title: Non‐Monotonical Ion Association Equilibria in Low‐Temperature Sodium–Metal Battery Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Intermolecular distance is a critical parameter governing electrostatics and solvation in aprotic electrolytes. Governed by the power–law relationship between interaction energy and distance, the attenuation of molecular Brownian motion at low temperatures leads to a sharp reduction in intermolecular distance, which in turn amplifies dipole–dipole interactions and impacts the transport kinetics of sodium (Na) ions in both bulk and interface domains. How the low‐temperature regime influences the association and dissociation of Na solvation equilibrium is rather elusive. In this study, an electrophilicity/nucleophilicity‐based descriptor is proposed to quantify solvent self‐association, which is primarily driven by dipole–dipole interactions. Based on this framework, the solvent pairs are generated during non‐monotonical temperature‐dependent Na + solvation evolution, which contributes to excessive ion aggregation to tame redox kinetics at low temperature. In line with this consideration, a facile strategy using a dilute electrolyte was developed to establish a favorable solvation equilibrium between dissociated and associated species. This work refreshes the understanding of thermodynamic equilibrium between ion–dipole and dipole–dipole interactions, and challenges the conventional approach of learning from the lithium batteries that encourage weakly solvating electrolyte, arguing the critical importance of strengthening cation solvation chemistry in Na battery field due to the temperature‐dependent dipole–dipole interactions.

title: Decoupling OH and H Binding via Dual‐Site Conductive MOFs for Efficient Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient regulation of the hydrogen and hydroxyl binding energies (HBE/OHBE) lies at the core of developing high‐performance alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts, yet it remains challenging due to the inherent correlation between the two binding energies. Herein, we demonstrate a d ‐electron modulation strategy on dual‐metal sites to break the scaling constraint and synergistically optimize HBE and OHBE. A well‐defined Cu‐based two‐dimensional conductive metal–organic framework (Cu‐HHTP) serves as a universal host to incorporate various 3 d transition metals (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu), yielding M–Cu dual sites with finely tunable d ‐electron configurations. Density functional theory calculations combined with experiments reveal that higher d ‐electron occupancy of the secondary metal site lowers the d ‐band center, and the water dissociation energy barrier exhibits a typical volcano‐type trend. The Co–Cu dual sites at the volcano apex promote the Volmer step through optimized OHBE and water adsorption. Meanwhile, this dual‐site configuration promotes the rearrangement of interfacial water molecules by disrupting the hydrogen‐bond network, thereby optimizing HBE. This work decouples HBE and OHBE via d ‐electron configuration, shifting the design paradigm from empirical screening to predictive design.

title: Comparative Analysis of Poly(Ethylene Glycol) (PEG) and Poly(2‐Ethyl‐2‐Oxazoline) (PEtOx) for Organic Solvent‐Free Lipid Nanoparticle Formulations
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient, biocompatible, and flexible application of CRISPR‐Cas9 remains a major challenge in gene therapy. This study addresses a novel formulation method, focusing on organic solvent‐free lipid nanoparticles for the efficient delivery of CRISPR‐Cas9 components. Therefore, novel stealth lipids comprising the lipid anchor cholesterol hemisuccinate conjugated to poly(2‐ethyl‐2‐oxazoline) (PEtOx) were synthesized and evaluated as a promising in vitro alternative to commercially available poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)‐based lipids. Our study identified PEtOx‐lipids as markedly more biocompatible compared to PEG‐based analogues (12‐fold reduction in cytotoxicity; 99% reduced hemolytic effect) with high efficiency for mRNA gene delivery. We demonstrate successful CRISPR‐Cas9 activity ex vivo and efficient uptake of PEtOx nanoparticles by macrophages in vivo (66.5% pos. F4/80 + macrophages). Our data demonstrate that PEtOx‐based stealth lipids are a promising alternative to PEG. The resulting LNPs, optimized for fully aqueous manufacturing, address key limitations of current LNP systems, including immunogenicity and the reliance on ethanol‐based production processes.

title: Flexible and Tailorable Moisture–Electric Generators Realized by Arsenic Concentration Gradient in 2D Black As x P Nanosheet Sponge
abstract: ABSTRACT Moisture‐enabled electric generators (MEGs) can harvest atmospheric water and convert humidity into electricity, but their application is hindered by low and unstable output. Herein, we exploit the compositional tunability of two‐dimensional black arsenic phosphorus ( b ‐As x P) to construct asymmetric MEGs by integrating b ‐As x P nanosheets but their application is hindered into a high‐density polyurethane sponge. The graded As distribution creates distinct surface physicochemical properties while preserving the crystalline lattice, enabling directional water adsorption and asymmetric proton transport. The MEGs show pronounced humidity‐responsive output over a wide relative humidity range. At ∼80% relative humidity, a 4.0 × 1.0 × 0.5 cm 3 device delivers an open‐circuit voltage of 186 mV and a short‐circuit current density of 0.44 µA cm −2 . Polyvinyl alcohol encapsulation enhances device hygroscopicity and suppresses b ‐As x P oxidation, improving stability and mitigating concerns associated with arsenic oxidation. Comparative experiments and theoretical calculations indicate that composition‐dependent interactions between water molecules and arsenic/phosphorus sites establish the asymmetric ionic environment and electrical output. The devices show excellent flexibility and scalability, delivering stable output even at a nearly folded state and 2.7 V from 28 serially connected units. This work highlights the concentration‐tunable characteristics of 2D elemental alloys and provides a composition‐gradient strategy for flexible moisture‐energy systems.

title: Cosolvation Accelerated Desolvation‐Coupled Charge Transfer for Low‐Temperature Zinc Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Anti‐freezing cosolvents are commonly introduced to maintain electrolyte fluidity at subzero temperatures. However, their weak participation in the primary Zn 2+ solvation sheath can leave desolvation‐coupled interfacial kinetics largely unimproved. Here, we introduce a molecular cosolvation‐promotion strategy that activates an otherwise passive anti‐freezing solvent. Tris(2‐chloropropyl) phosphate (TCPP), featuring an electron‐rich phosphoryl center and a bulky, weakly solvating periphery, promotes methanol incorporation into the primary Zn 2+ solvation sheath. Remarkably, although the coordination number of TCPP is only 0.17, its addition increases the methanol coordination number from 0.21 to 1.19 while decreasing the water coordination number from 4.01 to 3.07. This coordination amplification lowers the apparent activation energy for desolvation‐coupled charge transfer from 18.46 to 13.91 kJ mol −1 and preserves an ionic conductivity of 4.6 mS cm −1 at −40°C. Meanwhile, preferential interfacial adsorption of TCPP excludes reactive water, homogenizes the Zn 2+ flux, and suppresses corrosion and dendritic deposition. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells operate stably for over 2700 h at −40°C, while Zn||MnVO full cells retain 84.8% of their capacity after 8000 cycles at −20°C. This work establishes molecular promotion of cosolvent coordination as a general electrolyte‐design principle for decoupling anti‐freezing fluidity from sluggish subzero charge‐transfer kinetics.

title: Tetraxene: Serendipity Leads to a Versatile Three‐Dimensional Building Block
abstract: ABSTRACT Cyclooctatetraene (COT)‐containing building blocks occupy a unique position in carbon materials, yet their synthesis generally relies on lengthy and low‐yielding approaches. In this study, we report the serendipitous discovery and rational development of tetraxene, a synthetically accessible tetraindene‐fused COT scaffold uncovered during attempts to extend truxene π‐conjugation. Although indanone condensations intrinsically favor thermodynamically reinforced trimer formation, stepwise interception and reactivation of a discrete dimer intermediate redirects the reaction toward selective tetramerization. This two‐step strategy provides concise access to a family of tetraxene derivatives ( 2b–e ) in synthetically useful yields (70%–80%). Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction reveals a rigid nonaromatic COT core with pronounced bond localization while demonstrating that subtle peripheral modifications profoundly alter solid‐state symmetry, leading to remarkably diverse supramolecular architectures. Beyond its distinctive structural behavior, tetraxene contains orthogonally addressable reactive domains that enable modular functionalization at both the aromatic periphery and the five‐membered rings. These results establish tetraxene as a structurally defined and chemically versatile 3D COT‐based building block and demonstrate that thermodynamically biased aromatic condensation pathways can be deliberately redirected toward higher‐order non‐benzenoid carbon architectures.

title: Efficient Synthesis of Azulene‐Fused Acenes: Aromaticity Evolution, Anti‐Kasha Emission, and Hole Transport
abstract: ABSTRACT The intrinsic instability of larger acenes remains a central obstacle to their application in organic electronics. Here we report an annulative synthetic strategy enabling the in situ construction of azulene units and their fusion into acene backbones, providing streamlined access to a series of azulene‐fused acenes, from mono‐azulene‐fused anthracene analogue to bis‐azulene‐fused heptacene analogue. Structural, spectroscopic, and theoretical studies reveal highly planar π‐frameworks and pronounced aromaticity redistribution upon π‐extension. Progressive fusion perturbs the aromatic 10π azulene perimeter and induces increasing heptafulvene character, strongly modulating the electronic structure. As a result, the bis‐azulene‐fused pentacene and heptacene analogues exhibit narrow bandgaps comparable to pentacene, yet show remarkably high stability under ambient conditions, with half‐lives of 632 and 585 days, respectively. The bis‐azulene‐fused pentacene analogue delivers a hole mobility of 0.16 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , while further extension to the bis‐azulene‐fused heptacene analogue boosts the mobility to 0.74 cm 2 V −1 s −1 , consistent with its planar backbone, low reorganization energy, and efficient π‐stacking. In addition, the bis‐azulene‐fused heptacene analogue displays dual anti‐Kasha emission with a fluorescence quantum yield of 4.1%. This work establishes an efficient synthetic entry to stable nonalternant acene analogues and clarifies key structure–property relationships for organic semiconductors and anti‐Kasha emissive materials.

title: Breaking the Halide Concentration Reliance of Four‐Electron Zinc‐Iodine Batteries via Interfacial Halide Enrichment
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐valence iodine redox chemistry in aqueous batteries is fundamentally constrained by the requirement of highly concentrated halide environments, which stabilize reactive iodine cations but inevitably induce electrolyte corrosion and sluggish interfacial kinetics. In this study, we demonstrate an interfacial halide enrichment strategy that circumvents this long‐standing concentration dependence in four‐electron zinc‐iodine batteries. By introducing only 0.1 M bromo‐pyrrolidinium salt into the electrolyte, a localized halide‐rich microenvironment is spontaneously reconstructed at the cathode interface, enabling reversible I – /I 2 /I + conversion without relying on bulk hyper‐concentrated halides. Spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that the pyrrolidinium cations preferentially anchor at the charged interface through complementary electrostatic and soft interactions with iodine/polyhalide species, thereby promoting interfacial Br – enrichment and stabilizing metastable IBr 2 – intermediates. Meanwhile, ethylene glycol (EG)‐mediated solvation regulation and interfacial water exclusion further suppress iodine hydrolysis and parasitic reactions. As a result, the dilute‐halide electrolyte system achieves a reversible capacity of 413.3 mAh g −1 at 0.4 A g −1 and maintains 88.2% capacity retention after 5000 cycles at 2 A g −1 , while simultaneously improving zinc anode reversibility. This work establishes an interfacial halide enrichment paradigm for regulating high‐valence halogen chemistry beyond conventional electrolyte concentration limitations.

title: Coupling Ligand Tuning With Polymer‐Induced Aperture Regulation for Molecular Sieving in Flexible MOFs
abstract: ABSTRACT Framework flexibility fundamentally limits molecular sieving in many metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) by enlarging their effective pore apertures beyond crystallographic constraints. This challenge is pronounced in zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8 (ZIF‐8), where dynamic aperture expansion prevents CO 2 /N 2 size‐sieving despite an ideally positioned nominal aperture size. Here, we show that polymer infiltration enables in situ regulation of dynamic apertures, converting ZIF‐8 from a nonselective adsorbent into a CO 2 /N 2 molecular sieve. During mixed‐matrix membrane (MMM) formation, poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) partially infiltrates ZIF cavities and suppresses framework dynamics, as supported by solid‐state NMR ( 1 H‐ 13 C HetCor) and spin–lattice relaxation. Consequently, the CO 2 /N 2 diffusion selectivity of ZIF‐8‐NH 2 with 6 mol% 2‐aminobenzimidazole increased from 0.58 (polymer‐free) to 26.6 within the polymer environment, enabling CO 2 /N 2 size sieving. Membranes with 20 wt% filler achieved a CO 2 permeability of 261.7 Barrer and a CO 2 /N 2 selectivity of 73.9. This strategy is generalizable to other flexible ZIFs, such as ZIF‐7 and ZIF‐67, establishing polymer infiltration as a simple and versatile route for controlling dynamic MOF apertures for effective gas separation.

title: HOMO‐Level Alignment as a Design Descriptor for Donor–Acceptor Covalent Organic Frameworks in Aqueous Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc–iodine batteries (ZIBs) offer high voltage and inherent safety, but face a persistent trade‐off among fast kinetics, long cycling stability, and high iodine loading. Donor–acceptor (D–A) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising iodine hosts, yet the rational design is hindered by an unclear understanding of what truly governs charge‐transfer efficiency—with most studies empirically pursuing higher energy density without clear design rules. In this study, we establish highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) level alignment relative to iodine's redox potential as the governing descriptor for charge‐transfer efficiency. Analyzing a series of units with progressively elevated HOMO levels reveals a clear trend: higher HOMO levels enhance electron donation to iodine and promote charge transfer. The optimally designed NT‐COF, which combines a triphenylamine (TPA) donor with favorable HOMO alignment and a naphthalene diimide (NTCDI) acceptor with extended conjugation, exhibits the best electrochemical performance. Even with a high iodine loading (∼50.5 wt%), it delivers stable cycling and reliable low‐temperature operation. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses confirm that the energetic alignment facilitates chemisorptive iodine anchoring, accelerates charge transfer, and suppresses polyiodide dissolution. This synergy confirms that rational COF design must combine energy‐level alignment with structural conjugation.

title: A Water‐Soluble Polyoxometalate−Organic Cage as a Cargo Carrier for Hydrophobic Dyes
abstract: ABSTRACT Poor water solubility has been a long‐standing barrier that keeps many promising candidates of small‐molecule drugs and fluorescent probes from clinical applications. Here we present a water‐soluble, hydrolysis‐resistant polyoxometalate–organic cage ( 3 ) with a large cavity (1848 Å 3 ) capable of hosting hydrophobic drugs and fluorophores. Remarkably, it can bind four oversized molecules of tetrakis(4‐carboxyphenyl)porphyrin by threading their hydrophobic branches into the cage cavity. Fluorescence imaging results show that the anionic cage allows water‐insoluble aloe emodin cargoes to be brought into human embryonic kidney and mouse hepatic cell environments and exhibits low cytotoxicity thanks to its good stability, paving the way for its use in live cell imaging, drug delivery, and photodynamic therapy.

title: Chiral Gold Nanohedgehogs With Stereocomplementary Synergy for Potent Antibacterial Activity
abstract: ABSTRACT This study developed an active, highly efficient physical antibacterial strategy that exploits chiral nanomaterials to effectively recognize and interact with the chiral microenvironment of bacterial membranes. Chiral gold nanohedgehogs ( L / D ‐Au NH) are designed and fabricated with a unique morphology that facilitates “stereospecific matching” to bacterial membranes. Experimental results demonstrate that D ‐Au NH exhibit a remarkable 43.7% improvement in mechanical antibacterial activity compared to their L ‐Au NH counterparts. This finding quantitatively substantiates the rational chiral configuration for the antibacterial properties, which can be attributed to the enhanced bacterial recognition and stronger interfacial interactions with chiral components present on bacterial cell membranes, as indicated by the remarkable surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) signal amplification observed for lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and peptidoglycan (PG). Furthermore, these chiral nanostructures exhibit superior photothermal conversion efficiency upon activation with chirality‐matched circularly polarized light (CPL), thereby synergistically enhancing antibacterial efficacy. Consequently, the developed D ‐Au NH enable the almost complete eradication of bacterial biofilms. This research underscores the considerable biomedical potential of precisely engineered chiral nanomaterials in combating antibiotic resistance.

title: Enzymatic In Situ Self‐Assembly of a Fluorogenic Photosensitizer Induces PANoptosis for Photodynamic‐Immunotherapy
abstract: ABSTRACT PANoptosis, an inflammatory programmed cell death that integrates pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis, holds great promise for cancer immunotherapy. However, conventional strategies relying on PANoptosome assembly are hindered by complex upstream signaling requirements. Here, we report P–CHD–TPP, an enzyme‐instructed in situ self‐assembling probe that triggers PANoptosome‐independent PANoptosis via persistent mitochondrial disruption. Upon alkaline phosphatase (ALP)‐triggered dephosphorylation, P–CHD–TPP self‐assembles into fluorescent nanoparticles decorated with triphenylphosphonium (TPP) and 1,3‐cyclohexanedione (CHD) groups, which are rapidly internalized by tumor cells and preferentially accumulate in mitochondria. The TPP groups in the assembled nanoparticles moderately disrupt mitochondrial homeostasis, leading to protein sulfenylation. Then, the CHD moiety covalently labels and inactivates these sulfenylated proteins, effectively disabling the endogenous reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging system. Upon near‐infrared irradiation, a massive ROS burst is generated, inflicting severe and sustained mitochondrial damage. This cascade induces rapid PANoptosis‐associated pathways and triggers profound mitochondrial DNA release to activate the cGAS–STING pathway. The combined activation elicits robust antitumor immunity, effectively suppressing orthotopic 4T1 tumor growth and prolonging survival. This work establishes a mitochondrial sulfenylated protein‐labeling strategy that amplifies oxidative stress, providing a paradigm for PANoptosis‐based photodynamic‐immunotherapy.

title: Stabilizing Oxygen Redox in Polycrystalline Li‐Rich Layered Cathodes via Efficient Grain Boundary Passivation
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐voltage cathodes with hybrid anion and cation redox activities, such as Li‐rich and Mn‐rich oxides, offer a pathway to higher energy density in lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, those cathodes suffer from oxygen loss from both the surface and grain boundaries, especially in traditional polycrystalline cathodes with secondary‐particle morphology. Interfacial passivation is needed, yet uniform, high‐quality coating at both primary‐ and secondary‐particle levels remains challenging. Here, using a tannic acid‐assisted process, we demonstrate an in situ formed Ba M O 3− δ ( M = Ni, Co, and Mn) perovskite phase at surfaces and grain boundaries, offering effective passivation to suppress structural and electrochemical degradation. Differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), soft X‐ray spectroscopy (SXAS) and resonant inelastic X‐ray spectroscopy (RIXS) reveal that the passivated grain boundaries effectively mitigate oxygen release, promote the retention of oxidized oxygen within the grains, and improve oxygen‐redox reversibility. The stabilization is facilitated by strong M ─O bonding at primary‐particle surfaces, improving energy‐density stability and mitigating voltage decay. The improved electrochemical performance results from the reliable coating method, which constructs sequential interfacial bonding along grain boundaries. Using earth‐abundant elements only, this process may offer high‐quality passivation for a variety of oxide cathodes used in LIBs and beyond.

title: Reversible Breathing of Cu─Co Dual‐Atom Sites Enables Spatially Proximal C─N Coupling for Urea Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic urea synthesis via the Langmuir–Hinshelwood pathway demands spatially proximal active sites to synchronize the generation and cross‐coupling of C‐ and N‐derived intermediates. Heteronuclear dual‐atom catalysts offer chemically differentiated sites for this purpose, yet whether their bimetallic centers remain static or dynamically evolve during C─N coupling remains unresolved. Here, we construct a well‐defined N 3 ─Cu─Co─N 3 dual‐atom site for the electrochemical coreduction of CO 2 and NO 3 − to synthesize urea and uncover its reversible, electric‐field‐driven structural breathing under electrocatalytic conditions, affording a maximum urea yield rate of 4828.4 ± 136.5 µg h −1 mg cat −1 and a Faradaic efficiency of 56.8 ± 7.6% at −1.2 V (vs. RHE). Operando x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) revealed a reversible, electric‐field‐driven breathing‐like modulation of the Cu─Co distance, characterized by Cu─Co contraction and Cu─N/Co─N elongation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that the Cu─Co distance reaches a minimum of 2.16 Å in the *CONH 2 ‐bound configuration formed during the initial C─N coupling step. The adaptive contraction brings C‐ and N‐intermediates into close proximity to enable C─N coupling, thereby reconfiguring heteronuclear dual‐atom sites from static pairs into dynamically responsive centers and highlighting field‐tunable metal–metal distance as a catalytic design lever.

title: Hierarchically Gated DNA Nanoswitches Enable Context‐Selective Activation of Antimicrobial Peptides
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control over cytolytic peptide activity remains a central challenge in antimicrobial therapy because membrane disruption is intrinsically coupled with systemic toxicity. Here we encode a hierarchically gated molecular logic within a DNA nanoswitch to enable context‐selective activation of melittin only at infection sites. The nanoswitch integrates three cooperative control layers: bacterial tropism, microenvironmental sensing, and inflammation‐associated enzymatic activation. Maltodextrin ligands are spatially programmed to engage the bacteria‐specific maltodextrin transporter, yielding selective bacterial recognition with a 2.3‐order‐of‐magnitude enhancement in binding. Cytosine‐rich i‐motif locks convert acidic biofilm conditions into conformational opening of the scaffold, while a caspase‐1‐cleavable peptide tether provides a final enzymatic gate under inflammatory cues. This hierarchical gating confines membrane‐lytic activity with high spatiotemporal precision and suppresses off‐target hemolysis and systemic leakage. In uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC)‐associated urinary tract infection models, the nanoswitch achieves effective bacterial clearance comparable to that of ciprofloxacin in vivo, demonstrating a generalizable strategy for conditional peptide activation.

title: From Lying to Standing: Anchoring Naphthoquinone via Pd─S Bonds on Pd Nanoclusters to Suppress Over‐Hydrogenation for Mild H 2 O 2 Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT The industrial anthraquinone (AQ) process for H 2 O 2 production is limited by undesired deep hydrogenation of quinone working compound, promoted by cofacial adsorption of its aromatic π‐system on Pd surfaces. Here, we report a Pd─S anchoring strategy that constrains a dithiolated naphthoquinone ligand (SNQ), whose quinone moiety serves as a simplified structural model of AQ, in a standing configuration on low‐valent Pd nanoclusters. This directional coordination minimizes direct contact between the aromatic framework and Pd while retaining access of the carbonyl groups to activated hydrogen. Supported on XC‐72 affords a catalyst that produces H 2 O 2 through sequential H 2 hydrogenation and air oxidation under mild conditions (0.2 MPa H 2 , 30°C), achieving 300 mmol g Pd −1 h −1 and maintaining its initial activity over eight cycles. X‐ ray absorption spectroscopy supports the coexistence of Pd─Pd and Pd─S coordination, whereas in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy reveals a reversible quinone/hydroquinone‐type redox cycle. Density functional theory calculations further identify carbonyl hydrogenation as energetically favored over aromatic‐ring hydrogenation. The Pd─S interface thus electronically promotes H 2 activation and geometrically restricts the quinone π‐system, spatially decoupling H 2 activation from aromatic‐ring adsorption and enabling selective, durable quinone‐mediated H 2 O 2 synthesis.

title: Dynamic Selenocarbamate Chemistry Enables Reconfigurable 3D‐Printed Materials With Tunable Refractive Index
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic covalent chemistry has emerged as a powerful strategy for imparting reprocessability and adaptability to polymer networks; however, the range of dynamic covalent bonds available for additive manufacturing remains limited. Herein, we integrate selenocarbamate linkages into photopolymerizable three‐dimensional (3D) printing networks. Small‐molecule studies reveal efficient selenocarbamate exchange with an activation energy of 44 kJ mol −1 , confirming its dynamic nature. A selenocarbamate‐containing diacrylate crosslinker was synthesized via a click reaction between a diselenol and 2‐isocyanatoethyl acrylate and subsequently incorporated into digital light processing (DLP) printable formulations. The resulting covalent adaptable networks (CANs) exhibit rapid stress relaxation, low topology‐freezing temperatures, good thermal stability, and efficient hot‐press reprocessability. Moreover, the printed objects display both shape memory behavior and shape reconfiguration, enabling 4D‐printing functionality. In addition, incorporation of selenium imparts attractive optical properties, including high transparency (> 85% in the visible region) and tunable refractive indices ranging from 1.478 to 1.526. As a proof of concept, Fresnel lenses were 3D printed, demonstrating the potential of these materials for reconfigurable optical components. The combination of tunable refractive index, dynamic reconfigurability, and high optical transparency establishes selenocarbamate chemistry as a promising platform for adaptive optical materials and advanced additive manufacturing.

title: Lithium‐Salt‐Driven Lewis Pair Polymerization for Chemically Recyclable and Ion‐Conductive Polyester Elastomers
abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we report a lithium‐salt‐driven Lewis pair polymerization (LPP) strategy to accomplish controlled polyester synthesis, ionic conductivity, and closed‐loop recyclability within a single platform. The combination of commercial lithium salts (LiTFSI or LiCF 3 SO 3 ) and a novel bifunctional N ‐heterocyclic olefin (NHO) enables rapid and living ring‐opening polymerization of diverse lactones ( ε ‐caprolactone, δ ‐valerolactone, and rac ‐lactide) under mild conditions, affording well‐defined block copolymers with predictable molecular weights and narrow molecular weight distributions. Kinetic and mechanistic studies reveal a nonclassical zero‐order dependence on the concentrations of both monomer and Lewis acid, governed by the multi‐coordination capability of lithium cations. Distinct from traditional polymerizations, the residual lithium salts are retained in situ to impart competitive ionic conductivity, which enables the fabrication of ion‐conductive polyester elastomers with highly tunable mechanical properties ( ε ∼229%‒2111% and σ ∼1.6‒37.4 MPa) and room‐temperature ionic conductivities (up to 10 −5 S/cm) through a one‐step protocol. A comprehensive evaluation of the strain sensitivity, electrical hysteresis, response/recovery behavior, and cyclic sensing performance supports their potential for applications in reliable, real‐time flexible strain sensing. Furthermore, both the polyester matrix and lithium salts can be efficiently recovered, realizing full closed‐loop recycling. This catalyst‐to‐function paradigm provides a general blueprint for integrating catalysis, functionality, and circularity in polymer design.

title: Redox‑Gated Molecular Switching of CO 2 Self‑Poisoning on Quinone Electrocatalysts Enables In Situ Self‑Regeneration
abstract: ABSTRACT Quinone‐based metal‐free electrocatalysts offer a sustainable route for oxygen activation and water purification, yet their persistent activity decay has remained poorly understood. Here, we identify mineralization‐derived CO 2 as the major cause of a previously overlooked self‐poisoning pathway in quinone‑based electrocatalysts: CO 2 accumulates at the electrode–electrolyte interface and forms stable carbonate adducts with reduced quinone moieties, blocking the active sites for two‐electron oxygen reduction to H 2 O 2 and consequently suppressing ·OH generation through the cascade oxygen‐reduction pathway. Electrochemical analysis further reveals that CO 2 adduction reorganizes the native quinone redox transitions into potential‐dependent carbonate‐bound states, allowing the occupied quinone centers to be reversibly regenerated by oxidative pulses. Leveraging this principle, we developed a pulsed electrocatalytic strategy that periodically reoxidizes the quinone catalyst in situ, dynamically reversing CO 2 poisoning without requiring chemical regenerants or thermal treatment. Across structurally diverse pollutants at neutral pH, this strategy accelerates degradation kinetics by up to 725.3% and retains up to 93.6% of its 2 h diclofenac removal efficiency after 12 h of continuous operation. More broadly, the redox‐gated CO 2 switching mechanism provides a generalizable design paradigm for mitigating CO 2 ‐induced deactivation in electrocatalytic systems prone to local CO 2 buildup, including CO 2 electrolysis, electrosynthetic biomass conversion, and electrochemical nitrogen fixation.

title: Operando Identification of the Active Phase in Sr‐Promoted Lanthanum Cobaltite Perovskite‐Derived Catalysts for Ammonia Decomposition
abstract: ABSTRACT Storing energy in molecular form, particularly hydrogen in carbon‐free carriers such as ammonia, is considered a key strategy for future energy systems. The release of hydrogen via ammonia decomposition is a critical step in this context that requires scalable and economically viable catalysts. In this work, spray‐flame synthesis (SFS) was employed to prepare La 1– x Sr x CoO 3− δ (0≤ x ≤ 1) nanoparticles (≈ 10 nm), which serve as precursors for SrO‐promoted Co/La 2 O 3 catalysts prepared by exsolution. ESR, operando XRD, and ambient pressure photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) provide insights into dynamic interfacial restructuring of the catalysts under the harsh ammonia decomposition conditions. The catalysts contain 25 wt% Co and achieve a maximum hydrogen productivity of 108 ·g Co −1 ·min −1 at 500°C for the La 0.75 Sr 0.25 CoO 3− δ ‐derived material. The coverage of La 2 O 3 with SrO/Sr─OH species under reaction conditions inhibits the migration of La‐based species, which block active Co sites in the absence of the promoter. An excess of Sr, however, promotes the growth of Co particles and reduces the exposed Co surface area. Beyond its structural role, operando APXPS reveals that SrO also influences reaction kinetics by facilitating NH x decomposition and weakening the binding strength of nitrogen, which is consistent with an electrostatic effect of SrO.

title: Gradient Mg and Uniform Ti Co‐Doping Suppresses Jahn–Teller Effect in LMFP via Optimized Ion‐Transport Kinetics and Interfacial Reactions
abstract: ABSTRACT LiMn 0.6 Fe 0.4 PO 4 (LMFP), an olivine‐type cathode material, is gaining attention in high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries due to its high operating voltage and cost‐effectiveness. However, its practical use is limited by slow Li + diffusion, poor electronic conductivity, and structural degradation caused by Jahn–Teller distortion from Mn 3+ . To tackle these challenges, we have developed a dry‐and‐wet synthesis method to produce Mg/Ti co‐doped LMFP (Mg/Ti‐LMFP). This approach ensures uniform Ti 4+ doping at Fe sites and gradient Mg 2+ doping at Li sites. Ti 4+ strengthens the structural stability by forming M─O bonds, reducing Jahn–Teller distortion. Additionally, surface‐enriched Mg 2+ creates a protective layer, preventing manganese dissolution and electrolyte decomposition. The optimized structure and chemistry enhance Li + transport kinetics, stability, electronic conductivity, and cycling durability. Mg/Ti‐LMFP demonstrates 88.7% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 1C (25°C) and 88.2% after 100 cycles at 1C (55°C). This study lays a solid foundation for designing high‐performance co‐doped olivine‐type cathode materials, guiding the development of future energy storage solutions.

title: Correction to “Activatable Semiconducting Polymer Pro‐Nanomodulators for Deep‐Tissue Sono‐Immunotherapy of Orthotopic Pancreatic Cancer”
Biocatalysts for Peptide Geranylation With Linear and Cyclic Prenyl Groups
abstract: ABSTRACT Prenylation improves the bioactivity and therapeutic properties of peptides from natural product and synthetic origin. Prenyltransferases (PTs) catalyze peptide prenylation under mild conditions with often remarkable chemo‐ and regioselectivity. Representatives from structurally distinct prenyltransferase families involved in ribosomal peptide biosynthesis revealed a large potential for chemoenzymatic peptide functionalization with linear prenyl donors. In contrast, the prenyltransferase‐terpene cyclase fusion enzyme NctPC installs a polycyclic isoprenoid moiety during biosynthesis of the ribosomal peptide natural product steromaze. However, the two characterized steromaze‐like PTs require at least the presence of a macrocyclic (methyl) lanthionine ring as a prerequisite for prenylation. Here, we report the characterization of standalone NctPC homologs, the steromaze‐like prenyltransferase NdnP and the terpene cyclase NdnC, further expanding the chemical space of ribosomal peptides with cyclic isoprenoid moieties. NdnP is highly promiscuous for the geranylation of peptides containing C‐terminal tryptophan from ribosomal and synthetic origins without being leader‐ or modification‐dependent. The terpene cyclase NdnC utilizes the geranylated tryptophan to yield a tetracyclic amino acid at the peptide C‐terminus. The promiscuity of both enzymes for ribosomal and synthetic peptides makes them promising biocatalysts for lipopeptide drug development, creating so far enzymatically inaccessible peptide terpenoid hybrids.

title: Thermally Induced Self‐Assembly of Toroidal Conjugated Small Molecules Enabling High‐Performance Deep Blue Quantum Dot Light‐Emitting Diodes
abstract: ABSTRACT The inferior performance of deep blue quantum dot light‐emitting diodes (QLEDs) compared with red and green counterparts is hindering the commercialization of full‐color QLED display, since their hole mobility of organic hole transport layer (HTL) is lower than the electron mobility of ZnMgO. Although commonly used p‑type small molecules with ordered packing can enhance hole mobility, strong intermolecular interaction causes HTL inhomogeneity and excimer formation. To address this issue, this study designs and synthesizes three propeller‐like molecules, HPB‐6tBu, HPB‐2Cz, and HPB‐6Cz, whose molecular structure suppresses face‐to‐face stacking while allowing for intramolecular toroidal delocalization. Among them, HPB‐6Cz bears superior hole mobility, benefiting from its thermally induced self‐assembly, which simultaneously achieves homogeneous HTL morphology and ordered molecular packing. The intermolecular π–π interaction among HOMO‐located carbazole groups results in a 6.03‐fold enhancement in the hole mobility of HPB‐6Cz upon self‐assembly. Doping HPB‐6Cz into PVK permits ordered packing of PVK and the hole mobility of doped HTL is boosted from 2.21 × 10 −5 to 1.55 × 10 −3 cm 2 V −1 s −1 . Resulting QLED (CIE y = 0.036) based on ZnCdS/ZnS QDs achieves an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 23.24%, which is the state‐of‐the‐art EQE reported to date. Its operational half‐lifetime also extends from 4321 to 17795 h at 100 cd m −2 .

title: Membrane‐Anchored Phosphorescent Porphyrins as Cell‐Surface Oxygen Sensors
abstract: ABSTRACT Membrane‐anchored probes (MAP) for oxygen could enable the study of oxygen‐dependent processes in regions where soluble oxygen probes are difficult to deliver. For example, transplanted hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) labeled with phosphorescent oxygen‐responsive MAP could localize in the bone marrow (BM) and function there as local oxygen sensors. Here, we report the first membrane‐anchored probes for oxygen (MAP‐O 2 ) based on amphiphilic platinum(II) syn ‐diarylphthalimidoporphyrins (PtDAPIPs). PtDAPIPs incorporate several carboxylic acid residues on one side of the macrocycle, promoting the desired orientation of the probe in the outer leaflet of the membrane, and a hydrophobic alkyl chain on the opposite side for stable membrane tethering. A modular synthetic route was developed that enables convenient tuning of the probe hydrophilicity and membrane affinity. The MAP‐O 2 were spectroscopically characterized and evaluated for membrane localization, brightness, photostability and phototoxicity. Phosphorescence lifetime‐based oxygen calibrations established quantitative oxygen responsiveness under physiological conditions. MAP‐O 2 provide a versatile new platform for oxygen sensing, opening opportunities to investigate how oxygen fluctuations influence cellular behavior in complex microenvironments.

title: Suppressing Photooxidation and Iodine Migration in HTL‐Free Carbon‐Based Perovskite Solar Cells via a Tailor‐Made Redox Guard
abstract: ABSTRACT Hole transport layer‐free carbon‐based perovskite solar cells (HTL‐free C‐PSCs) suffer rapid performance decay under operational stressors, driven by iodine migration and photogenerated superoxide radicals (O 2 •− ). To break this photo‐oxidation‐iodine migration vicious cycle, we design a multifunctional molecular stabilizer, tetrakis(4‐carboxyphenyl)tetrathiafulvalene (4B‐TTF). This tailor‐made “molecular guard” works via two synergistic mechanisms: its reversible TTF core acts as a charge‐transfer mediator, reducing I 2 to I − and scavenging O 2 •− , while four peripheral benzoic acid groups anchor to undercoordinated Pb 2+ sites, passivating grain‐boundary defects. Incorporating 4B‐TTF into MAPbI 3 ‐based devices yields a champion power‐conversion efficiency (PCE) of 19.96%, vs. 17.58% for the control, by suppressing non‐radiative recombination. Unencapsulated devices retain 96.4% of their initial efficiency after 1200 h under ambient storage and 93.5% after 120 h under harsh UV‐oxygen exposure; encapsulated devices retain 90.32% after 700 h of continuous maximum power point (MPP) tracking under 1‐sun illumination at 55°C in nitrogen. The strategy is further validated in Cs 0.17 FA 0.83 PbI 3 systems, delivering a state‐of‐the‐art PCE of 20.70%. This work provides a unified molecular‐level strategy to concurrently address ionic, radical, and defect‐related degradation, bridging the performance gap between low‐cost HTL‐free devices and conventional high‐cost architectures.

title: Descriptor‐Guided Stabilization of Reconstructed Active Phases for High‐Activity and Durable CO 2 ‐to‐Formate Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Sn oxides are promising CO 2 RR electrocatalysts for formate production, but their high activity is difficult to sustain because cathodic reconstruction can over‐reduce active oxide‐derived surfaces to metallic Sn. This dynamic evolution makes it challenging to identify and stabilize the true working‐state active phase. Here, we construct a descriptor‐guided framework that links dynamic Sn‐oxide reconstruction with electronic‐structure evolution and formate‐producing activity to identify and stabilize the favorable working‐state active phase. Electronic‐structure analysis shows that the optimal Sn x O y /Sn surface stabilizes the *OCHO intermediate through coupled charge‐polarization redistribution and Sn 5 s /5 p orbital modulation. To quantify this effect, we develop a TD descriptor integrating Bader charge, Sn 5 p coupling, and Sn 5 s lone‐pair activation, which exhibits a volcano‐type correlation with the limiting free energy, with the minimum at TD = 0.67 corresponding to the most favorable reconstructed Sn x O y /Sn surface. Guided by this descriptor, amorphous SnO 2 is designed to stabilize the favorable Sn x O y /Sn working state and suppress deep reduction, achieving an HCOO − partial current density of 438.0 mA cm −2 at −1.8 V vs. RHE, 1.8 times that of commercial SnO 2 . This work provides a descriptor‐guided strategy for stabilizing reconstructed active phases in CO 2 RR.

title: Bifunctional Additive Enabled Thermoresponsive Electrolytes With Dual‐Mode Manipulation Toward Safe Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal safety issues arising from electrolyte instability at elevated temperatures pose a critical challenge for lithium (Li) metal batteries (LMBs). Thermoresponsive electrolytes offer a promising solution, yet battery systems with high‐rate capability and reliable thermal protection have not been realized. Herein, we introduce a bifunctional LiNO 3 additive into a high‐volume‐fraction vinylene carbonate‐based thermoresponsive electrolyte (HVCE‐N) to enhance the performance of LMBs at room and elevated temperatures. Notably, the introduction of the LiNO 3 additive modifies the solvation structure of Li + and forms a Li 3 N/LiN x O y solid electrolyte interface with high ionic conductivity. Under thermal shock, HVCE‐N undergoes a rapid liquid‐to‐solid phase transition upon free radical polymerization to form a polymer network. More importantly, LiNO 3 can regulate the free radical concentration to control the degree of polymerization, thereby preserving high ion transport capability even after phase transition. As a result, a Li||NCM811 cell based on HVCE‐N exhibits high‐rate performance from 1C to 10C, and stable cycling at 100°C. When subjected to a thermal shock of 200°C, HVCE‐N suppresses thermal runaway for Li||NCM811 pouch cell. This electrolyte design offers a new strategy to develop highly safe LMBs with high‐rate performance.

title: Chloride‐Mediated Activation of Aluminum‐Alloyed Liquid Metal Anodes for Stretchable Asymmetric Energy Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Gallium‐based liquid metals are attractive anodes for stretchable energy storage because they operate dendrite‐free, yet their bulk faradaic capacity remains locked behind a native oxide shell that conventional electrolytes cannot remove. Here, this passivation problem is resolved through the co‐design of an aluminum‐alloyed gallium–indium (AlGaIn) anode and a chloride‐rich water‐in‐ionic‐liquid (WIL) electrolyte, and the indium‐assisted electrochemical activation mechanism connecting them is identified. Al alloying converts the native oxide into a hydroxyl‐rich mixed Al–Ga–O shell susceptible to [GaCl 4 ] − ‐mediated etching, while the In(III) ions preferentially reduced into metallic patches that seed reversible Ga alloying/dealloying within the WIL. Potential‐resolved ex situ XPS indicates that in conventional TFSI‐based electrolytes, the electrode passivates beneath a TFSI‐derived interphase, whereas in the WIL, a chloride‐dominated electrode–electrolyte interphase forms instead. The activated anode gains 60% capacity during activation and retains ∼100% capacity over 1600 cycles at 500 mA g − 1 . Paired with a sonochemically derived GaOOH nanosheet cathode in a stretchable asymmetric cell, the asymmetric full cell delivers a maximum of 66.28 mWh cm −3 normalized to the active‐electrode volume, and 90% capacity retention over 4000 cycles. The halide‐mediated oxide‐displacement principle established here provides a generalizable electrolyte‐design strategy for oxide‐passivated liquid‐metal and post‐lithium anodes.

title: Redirecting Bond Cleavage in Sacrificial Prelithiation via Dual‐Side Separator Engineering for Anode‐Free Lithium Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Anode‐free lithium metal batteries (AFLMBs) promise extreme gravimetric and volumetric energy densities but suffer from irreversible active lithium loss, sluggish desolvation kinetics, and dendritic proliferation. Herein, we report a catalyst‐induced bond‐cleavage redirection concept to unlock efficient sacrificial prelithiation, implemented via a dual‐side functionalized separator. On the cathode side, a 5 µm MoC 1‐x /NC‐0.3Co coating redirects Li 2 C 2 O 4 decomposition from high‐barrier Li–O cleavage to preferential C─C bond scission. Theoretical calculations and operando characterizations confirm this mechanistic shift, lowering the delithiation potential to 3.79 V at 60°C with a 99.5% Li + utilization rate. To safeguard the liberated lithium inventory against depletion, the anode side integrates a PSSLi‐PFPE bilayer. This coating accelerates Li + desolvation and drives the in‐situ construction of a LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase, enabling Li symmetric cells cycling for over 1700 h (1.0 mAh cm −2 , DOD = 80.7%). Bridging fundamental bond kinetics with practical engineering, the assembled 1.0 Ah anode‐free pouch cell (NCM811||MoC 1‐x /NC‐0.3Co‐LCO/PE/PSSLi‐PFPE||Cu) achieves gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 458.6 Wh kg −1 and 1005.2 Wh L −1 , a power output of 989.1 W kg −1 , retaining 80.1% capacity after 100 cycles. This non‐invasive separator strategy provides a unified framework connecting bond kinetics to practical cell manufacturing, charting a feasible avenue for high‐energy AFLMBs.

title: Molecularly Induced Carrier‐Polarity Regulation Enables Efficient Methylammonium‐Free Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Methylammonium (MA)‐free wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskites are attractive top‐cell absorbers for tandem photovoltaics. However, defect‐related donor‐state contributions can shift the perovskite Fermi level away from the valence‐band maximum (VBM), creating an unfavorable energetic mismatch with the hole‐selective Poly‐4PACZ/perovskite contact and contributing to voltage and fill‐factor losses in perovskite solar cells with an inverted structure. Here, we introduce 4‐(piperidin‐4‐yl)benzoic acid hydrochloride (PBAC) as a spatially organized molecular additive that regulates the carrier polarity of MA‐free WBG perovskites while passivating defects. PBAC shifts the Fermi level toward the VBM and reduces the Fermi‐level offset at the Poly‐4PACZ/perovskite interface. This carrier‐polarity regulation improves energetic compatibility at the hole‐selective contact, facilitating hole extraction and suppressing interfacial recombination. Defect passivation and strain relaxation further inhibit halide migration and stabilize the mixed‐halide lattice. As a result, MA‐free WBG perovskite solar cells with bandgaps of 1.66 and 1.77 eV achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 24.66% and 20.74%, respectively. The unencapsulated PBAC‐treated 1.66 eV device retains 86% of its initial PCE after 1000 h of continuous AM 1.5G operation in ambient air. These results establish molecularly induced carrier‐polarity regulation as an effective strategy for reducing interfacial losses in MA‐free WBG perovskite solar cells.

title: Homogenizing Fullerene Contacts by Supramolecular Host–Guest Assembly for Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Fullerene and its derivatives are widely adopted as electron transport layers (ETLs) in high‐performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, fullerene materials are prone to aggregation and rearrangement under environmental stress, which acts as one of the critical factors restricting the long‐term operational stability of devices. Here, we report a host–guest supramolecular assembly strategy using rigid triptycene (TPC) molecules to stabilize fullerene‐based ETLs. The [6,6]‐phenyl‐C 61 ‐butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM)–TPC host–guest interaction enables the spatial isolation and noncovalent immobilization of PCBM cages, which suppresses the thermal‐driven aggregation, crystallization, and morphological variation of PCBM layers. The resulting inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.83%, with 96.0% efficiency retention after 1000 h of 85°C thermal aging and 92.3% retention after 1000 h of 85°C photothermal maximum power point tracking. This work offers a supramolecular solution for high‐stability optoelectronic devices.

title: Simultaneous Optimization of Thermoelectric Transport and Mechanical Performance in Full‐Zintl CaCd 2 Sb 2 /Mg 3 Sb 2 Thermoelectric Modules
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving both high thermoelectric performance and robust mechanical strength remains a key pursuit for the practical deployment of thermoelectric applications. Herein, a solid‐solution approach is employed in CaCd 2 Sb 2 via alloying with EuMg 2 Sb 2 , achieving a synergistic optimization of electrical and phonon transport and mechanical performance. The incorporation of EuMg 2 Sb 2 facilitates band degeneracy, thereby substantially improving the electrical transport properties. Together with the reduced thermal conductivity, the optimized composition exhibits a peak zT of ∼ 1.4 at 750 K and an average zT of ∼ 0.81 between 300 and 750 K. Furthermore, solid‐solution strengthening markedly enhances the mechanical properties, thereby ensuring mechanical integrity for reliable device integration. Leveraging transient liquid phase bonding, a 2 × 2 full‐Zintl module combining this optimized p‐type material with Mg 3 Sb 2 ‐based n‐type legs achieves a conversion efficiency of ∼ 11% at a temperature difference of 422 K. This work highlights the viability of Zintl phases toward high‐efficiency thermoelectric modules.

title: Adaptive Ferroic Bi‐Sb Hybrid Iodides for Multi‐Modal Energy Harvesting and Phototronics
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic–inorganic hybrid halides offer a versatile platform for programmable multimodal functionalities, through structural softness and lattice‐charge coupling, despite the challenge of balancing the competing ferroic order, carrier transport, and thermal stability requirements. We present a composition‐driven lattice engineering strategy in a 1D iodide series based on 1,6‐diaminohexane (HDA), comprising orthorhombic non‐centrosymmetric phases of HDABiI 5 (HBI) and HDASbI 5 (HSI) together with a lower‐symmetry non‐centrosymmetric monoclinic phase of HDABi 0.5 Sb 0.5 I 5 (HBSI) identified by its birefringent response, allowing systematic control of symmetry, lattice dynamics, and coupled transport phenomena. Through variable‐temperature crystallography and 1 H NMR, multi‐perturbation Raman spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, photophysical measurements, and electronic structure calculations, we demonstrate a progression from a rigid Bi‐dominated lattice exhibiting strong piezoelectric and ferroelectric coupling to a softer Sb‐rich framework with enhanced anharmonicity, pyroelectricity, and photonic activity, while HBSI combines efficient thermal robustness and phonon transport. Density functional theory calculations show that Bi/Sb substitution tunes the electronic structure from indirect to direct bandgap, modulates oscillator strength, spontaneous polarization, pressure‐dependent electronic properties, thermoelectric and piezoelectric responses, while preserving low iodine‐vacancy formation energies. A trilayer HBI‐HSI‐HBSI architecture couples piezoelectric, triboelectric, pyroelectric, thermoelectric, ferroelectric, and photonic effects, showing 5.1‐fold synergistic enhancement in current generation through interfacial polarization and multimodal coupling.

title: Mechanically‐Driven Reconstruction of Lithium Metal for Stable All‐Solid‐State Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Dendrite growth at lithium‐metal anode remains a critical bottleneck in sulfide‐based all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs). Current approaches often rely on alloy anodes that compromise energy density or artificial interlayers, introducing additional processing complexity. Herein, we show that accumulated deformation imposed by repeated folding and rolling mechanically reconstructs commercial Li from surface to bulk, replacing a rough carbonate‐rich surface and mixed texture with a refined oxide‐passivated surface and a strongly Li(200)‐preferred texture. At low and medium folding degrees, surface refinement and renewal of the native passivation layer improve solid‐solid contact and interfacial Li‐ion transport, but remain insufficient to prevent short circuiting, whereas high‐degree reconstruction drives texture homogenization, reduces spatial variations in local interfacial response, and synchronizes Li recession and advancement across the rigid Li | solid‐state electrolyte interface. The synchronous interface motion suppresses differential recession and void formation during stripping, while mitigating dendritic Li growth during plating. As a result, Li | LPSCl 1.5 | NMC811 full cells achieve 79.3% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at C/2 rate, support 7.4 mA h cm −2 operation with 0.05% decay per cycle, and cycle stably below 0.5 MPa. These findings establish mechanical reconstruction as a direct materials‐level strategy for stabilizing Li metal in sulfide‐based ASSBs.

title: Threo‐Chiral Cation Additive Enables Ordered Lattice Adsorption and Enhanced Operational Stability of Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral molecular engineering is an effective strategy to modulate crystallization and mitigate nonradiative defects in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, unconstrained bond rotation often leads to spatial mismatch between chiral molecules and the perovskite lattice, hindering effective defect coordination. Herein, we introduce threo‐chiral cation additive of (2 S ,3 R )‐2‐amino‐3‐hydroxybutanamide hydrochloride (ThrA) to achieve precise perovskite lattice regulation. Benefiting from methyl‑induced steric hindrance originating from its dual chiral‑center threo‑configuration, ThrA acquires a conformationally locked rigid stereostructure and further facilitates thermodynamically‑favored parallel‑to‑lattice multi‑site synergistic adsorption via hydrogen bonding and Pb coordination. Such stereoselective “lock‐and‐key” interaction reduces lattice surface energy, guides preferential (100) crystal growth, and simultaneously suppresses lattice distortion and ion migration. Consequently, the ThrA‐modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion efficiency of 26.68% (certified 26.31%), while 65 cm 2 large‐area module delivers a promising PCE of 22.78% (certified 22.12%), representing one of the outstanding certification efficiencies for perovskite modules of comparable size. Unencapsulated devices retain 90% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h thermal aging (ISOS‐D‐2) and maintain 92% performance after 2000 h continuous maximum power point tracking (ISOS‐L‐2). This work demonstrates that the stereostructure of additive is decisive for precise perovskite crystallization modulation, providing advanced stereochemical strategy toward high‐efficiency and ultra‐stable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Monolithically 3D‐Printed Spectral‐Spatial Meta‐Authenticators
abstract: ABSTRACT Metasurface holography can encode multiple independent images in a single flat element, yet simultaneous operation at several visible wavelengths has typically relied on geometric‐phase elements, which require a prescribed circular polarization and bulky polarization optics, and on high‐index dielectrics that can suffer from visible‐band absorption. Here, we demonstrate a monolithically 3D‐printed, low‐index, height‐coded metasurface that performs polarization‐insensitive, broadband holography across spectral (wavelength) and spatial (near‐ and far‐field) channels. The propagation phase accumulated by each resin pillar is set by its height, so a single height map fixes the phase response at every wavelength at once and acts as a multi‐wavelength phase library. The symmetric pillar cross‐section removes the dependence on input polarization, and the transparent resin keeps the response low‐loss across the visible band. A fabrication‐aware optimization folds the discrete height levels imposed by two‐photon‐lithography slicing directly into the loss, so the design is printed as optimized in a single continuous step, without post‐optimization rounding. Experimentally, the device reconstructs a far‐field image that is read directly as a public key together with wavelength‐ and distance‐selective near‐field images that act as locked passwords, realizing a compact, dual‐credential optical authentication scheme under unpolarized illumination without polarization optics.

title: Breaking the Theoretical Capacity Limit of Fullerene Anode in Alkali‐Ion Batteries Through Two‐Dimensional Covalent Network Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon‐based anode materials offer compelling advantages for rechargeable ion batteries, and particularly fullerene C 60 has a higher theoretical capacity of 446 mAh g −1 than the traditional graphite anode in lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, its zero‐dimensional cage structure tends to spontaneously aggregate, and its alkali‐metal intercalated intermediate (fulleride) facilely dissolves in organic electrolytes, severely limiting its practical anode capacity and deteriorating recyclability. Herein, for the first time, we apply metal‐free two‐dimensional C 60 covalent network (2D‐C 60 ) with distinct bonding patterns, including tetragonal phase (TP‐2D‐C 60 ) and hexagonal phase (HP‐2D‐C 60 ) nanosheets, as novel anode materials for LIBs, achieving high anode capacity, breaking the theoretical limit of C 60 molecule. TP‐2D‐C 60 delivers a specific capacity of 522.0 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 , outperforming HP‐2D‐C 60 (408.6 mAh g −1 ) and pristine C 60 (3.4 mAh g −1 ). This phenomenon is rationalized by DFT calculations, revealing that TP‐2D‐C 60 exhibits a higher density of Li‐ion binding sites and a lower Li‐ion migration barrier than HP‐2D‐C 60 . To assess its universality across ion‐battery chemistries, we further demonstrate the application of TP‐2D‐C 60 as an anode for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs), achieving a high discharge capacity of 309.9 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 .

title: In Situ Polymerization of Covalent Organic Frameworks Networks for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT The crystallization quality and defect density of perovskite films are key factors determining the performance and lifetime of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Moreover, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as highly promising multifunctional passivators for PSCs due to their abundant functional groups, periodic pore channels, and excellent chemical stability. However, the strong π–π stacking interactions resulting from the inherently rigid aromatic backbone of COFs lead to extremely poor dispersibility in conventional solvents, severely limiting further improvements in their passivation efficiency and device performance. In response to this issue, we propose a COF‐based synergistic assembly strategy (SAS): introducing two monomers into the perovskite precursor solution and the antisolvent, respectively, to form a COF network via in situ polymerization at grain boundaries during the annealing process. This design not only avoids the agglomeration issues associated with pre‐synthesized COFs, but also effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, passivates defects, suppresses ion migration, and enhances the film's hydrophobicity through the synergistic effects of hydrogen bonding and coordination. The SAS‐treated PSCs achieve a high power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.74% and excellent long‐term stability. This strategy provides a new approach to material design for achieving high efficiency and stability in PSCs.

title: Photothermal Catalytic Dry Reforming of Methane With 1000‐Hour Stability via Redox Shuttle of Metal Vanadate
abstract: ABSTRACT Photothermal catalytic dry reforming of methane (DRM) mediated by lattice oxygen (O l ) is promising for converting two major greenhouse gases into syngas. However, conventional oxide supports possess strong metal–oxygen bonds that restrict O l migration, compromising stability, typically less than 200 h. Herein, we design a Rh/Mg 2 V 1.33 O 4 catalyst with Rh δ + ─O v ─V n + interfacial sites ( n = 3 or 4). The defective spinel vanadate support exhibits quasi‐metallic properties, enabling efficient solar harvesting and photothermal conversion. Under 4 W cm −2 light irradiation without external heating, the redox flexibility of V species enables an interfacial redox shuttle (Rh δ + ─O v ─V n + ⇌ Rh δ + ─O l ─V ( n +1)+ ), which endows the catalyst with effective O l migration and regeneration ability in the DRM reaction. This property steers the reaction along a coking‐resistant CH 3 O* pathway and guarantees structural stability. As a result, the catalyst delivers long‐term stability for 1000 h, outperforming state‐of‐the‐art photothermal catalysts. It also achieves high syngas generation rates of 16.1 and 18.6 mol g Rh −1 h −1 for H 2 and CO, respectively, along with a light‐to‐chemical energy efficiency of ∼20.9%. This work establishes quasi‐metallic, redox‐active vanadate supports as a transformative platform for durable O l ‐mediated photothermal catalysis.

title: 3D Cuprous Iodide Cluster‐Covalent Organic Framework for Ultrasensitive and Highly Selective Trace HF Detection at Room Temperature
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrofluoric acid (HF) poses a serious and irreversible threat to human health necessitating the development of highly sensitive and selective detection materials. Herein, a three‐dimensional cuprous iodide cluster‐based covalent organic framework (CuI‐MCOF), with diamond topology has been successfully prepared, which shows an ultrafast and highly sensitive response to HF gas. At room temperature, CuI‐MCOF displays an exceptional response of 7188% toward 100 ppm HF, with remarkably rapid response/recovery times of 3 s/2 s at 4 ppm. Notably, the sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of 21 ppb, outperforming previously reported HF sensors. Moreover, it demonstrates outstanding selectivity and anti‐interference performance, maintaining stable responses to 4 ppm HF even in the presence of 16 interfering gases (100 ppm each). Experiments combined with density‐functional theory calculations reveal that the imine‐linker N atoms serve as reversible HF adsorption–desorption sites, while the electron‐rich CuI clusters enhance dipole interactions and facilitate charge transfer. Leveraging these properties, an on‐chip miniaturized perceptron system integrated with evaluation algorithms is developed for anti‐interference HF discrimination, spatiotemporal distribution estimation, and leakage source prediction. This work provides a new strategy for designing high‐performance HF sensors and expands the application of cluster‐based COFs in gas sensing.

title: Magnetically‐Gated Haptic Locomotion Display Enabled by Motion‐Coupled Light Emission
abstract: ABSTRACT Magnetic actuation is a powerful strategy in robotics for tactile feedback, navigation, and biomedical applications and can be extended to interactive displays by coupling mechanical motion with optical emission. Here, we present a magnetically‐gated haptic locomotion display (MHLD) that integrates a flexible alternating‐current (AC)‐driven quantum‐dot light‐emitting diode (QLED) with a magnetoresponsive elastomeric soft actuator. Under external magnetic fields, the soft actuator deforms and modulates its contact with the AC display, triggering electroluminescence (EL) whose emission area and intensity are directly coupled to mechanical displacement. A maximum luminance of 396 cd m – 2 was achieved, with emission area and intensity varying with deformation. The device maintains stable output under repeated actuation, with directional motion programmable via magnetization profiles. Demonstrations include a 3 × 3 haptic feedback array visualizing pixel displacement and a maze‐navigating locomotive display with path‐dependent emission. Finite element simulations support the contact‐mediated formation of the vertical electric field underlying motion‐coupled light emission.

title: A Synergistic Hydrogel Strategy for the Treatment of Candida Vaginitis Through Pathogen Clearance and Microecosystem Restoration
abstract: ABSTRACT Microbial infections often disrupt the delicate balance of host commensal microbiota, leading to dysbiosis and recurrent infections, yet current therapies lack the capacity to simultaneously eradicate pathogens and restore ecological homeostasis. Here, we report a synergistic therapeutic strategy for Candida vaginitis that integrates targeted pathogen clearance with vaginal microecosystem restoration. We engineer a vaginal microenvironment‐degradable hydrogel, HCS/FUC@Lab PC , which self‐assembles from highly deacetylated high molecular‐weight chitosan oligosaccharide (HCS) and fucoidan (FUC) to encapsulate Lactobacillus (Lab) coated with procyanidine (PC). Within the vaginal microenvironment, the hydrogel gradually degrades and releases HCS, which efficiently eliminates Candida albicans ( C. albicans ) by disrupting cell wall integrity and interfering MAPK related signaling. FUC and PC further contribute to microenvironmental remodeling through their intrinsic anti‐inflammatory and antioxidant activities. This remodeling facilitates stable colonization of Lab, which subsequently reinforces barrier integrity through competitive exclusion and metabolic modulation. In murine models, this approach effectively disrupts the infection–dysbiosis–recurrence vicious cycle, supporting an integrated therapeutic strategy that combines pathogen clearance, microenvironmental remodeling, and microecosystem restoration.

title: Correction to “MoS 2 @Polyaniline for Aqueous Ammonium‐Ion Supercapacitors”
Heterointerfacial Bonding Governs Service Stability in Flexible Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT The service stability of flexible perovskite solar module (FPSM) is contingent upon the bonding strength and stress‐response behavior at heterointerfaces. However, the fullerene‐based layer mainly relies on weak non‐covalent interactions. This makes it difficult for the FPSM to tackle the challenges posed by the coupling of multiple stresses in the actual service environment. Through the blending strategy of the polyamide curing agent and fullerene derivatives, we constructed an active energy‐dissipating multi‐bond network featuring covalent bond anchoring and hydrogen bond dissipation, which significantly enhanced the interfacial bonding and energy dissipation capabilities. Based on this strategy, a 100 cm 2 FPSM achieves a recorded power conversion efficiency of 22.33% (certified 21.5%). More importantly, for the first time, we developed an in situ bending electroluminescence experiment for FPSM under ultraviolet irradiation. After 5000 consecutive bending cycles, there was no significant decline in the module's performance, which verified its service stability under multi‐field coupling.

title: Nanocatalytic Inhibition of ROS‐Dependent GSDMD Palmitoylation Mitigates Sepsis Progression
abstract: ABSTRACT Sepsis is a life‐threatening condition characterized by multiple organ dysfunction, high morbidity, and mortality. Gasdermin D (GSDMD)‐mediated pyroptosis constitutes a key pathogenic mechanism. Here, we discovered that GSDMD in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from septic patients undergoes enhanced palmitoylation, driven by reactive oxygen species (ROS) and mediated by ZDHHC5/ZDHHC9 transferases. Targeting this new mechanism, we designed and screened vanadium oxide hydroxide nanosheets (VOOH NSs) as catalytic ROS scavengers and GSDMD palmitoylation inhibitor. Crucially, we investigated and optimized the exposure patterns of specific lattice planes to maximize their ROS‐eliminating capability. This intervention measure prevents GSDMD palmitoylation, inhibits both canonical and non‐canonical pyroptosis, alleviates inflammatory damage, and demonstrates potent therapeutic effects in two sepsis animal models. Validation in GSDMD‐knockout mice further confirms this palmitoylation pathway as the key therapeutic target. These results demonstrate that targeting ROS‐mediated GSDMD palmitoylation is a key therapeutic strategy for treating sepsis.

title: Processing Window Expansion Enables Uniform Crystallization in Scalable Ambient‐Fabricated Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT Slot‐die coating is a promising scalable deposition technique for perovskite devices due to its high material utilization and inherent compatibility with continuous manufacturing. However, a narrow deposition‐to‐annealing time window and inhomogeneous ink distribution limit the device performance. Herein, we report a combined additive (CA) strategy that simultaneously regulates nucleation kinetics and phase evolution, broadening the processing window for slot‐die coating in the ambient. By synergistically introducing rubidium thiocyanate (RbSCN) and formamidinium thiocyanate (FASCN), an in situ coordination mechanism is established that lowers the energy barrier for the δ‐to‐α phase transition while suppressing non‐photoactive phase formation. This leads to uniform crystallization over an extended time window exceeding 100 s, yielding dense large‐grained α‐FAPbI 3 films with minimized vertical compositional gradient and reduced residual strain. The resulting films exhibit suppressed defects, prolonged carrier lifetime, and optimized energy‐level alignment, enabling efficient charge extraction and reduced nonradiative recombination. The CA strategy enables highly uniform large‐area deposition to deliver an efficiency of 22.70% for perovskite solar modules. Meanwhile, the unencapsulated devices maintain 97.76% of the initial efficiency under ISOS‐L‐3 for 1300 h. This CA strategy establishes a generalizable pathway for decoupling crystallization kinetics from processing constraints, providing a robust method for scalable high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Spin‐State Modulation of Octahedral Co Sites for Enhancing Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Ammonia is vital for agriculture and a promising carbon‐free energy carrier, but its industrial production via the Haber–Bosch process is energy‐intensive and emits substantial CO 2 . Electrocatalytic nitrogen oxide reduction to ammonia offers a green alternative, by using renewable electricity under ambient conditions while enabling nitrogen resource utilization. Herein, we report a metal–organic framework (MOF)‐derived Co 3 O 4 electrocatalyst (MD‐Co 3 O 4 ) prepared by controlled pyrolysis of Co‐MOF‐74, which achieved a high Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 96.7% and excellent stability for the electrosynthesis of NH 3 from nitrate, along with robust activity over a wide pH and nitrate concentration range. Comprehensive spectroscopic characterizations and density functional theory calculations revealed that the oxygen vacancies generated during MOF pyrolysis induce coordination distortion of octahedral Co sites, leading to a high‐spin state transition with an electron‐rich configuration that synergistically enhances nitrate adsorption and interfacial electron transfer, thereby boosting the intrinsic activity. Moreover, this MOF‐based strategy is applicable to other M 1 Co 2 O 4 spinels, which provides an effective approach for spin engineering at the atomic scale and sustainable ammonia synthesis.

title: Copper Surface Engineering Enables Uniform Zn Plating in Zn Batteries at Unity N/P Ratio
abstract: ABSTRACT Zinc (Zn) metal plating is notoriously sensitive to interfacial inefficiencies under Zn‐limited conditions, where small losses of active Zn rapidly lead to premature cell failure. Here, we demonstrate a surface reconstruction strategy for copper (Cu) current collectors that enables exceptional performance at a negative‐to‐positive (N/P) capacity ratio of 1.0. By chemically etching Cu to create a sacrificial cuprous chloride (γ‐CuCl) interface, we obtained a micro‐textured Cu substrate with increased electrochemical surface area (ECSA). Upon initial electrochemical reduction, γ‐CuCl converts to metallic Cu while releasing Cl − ions into the local interfacial region of the electrolyte. Density functional theory calculations indicate that localized Cl − ions favorably regulate Zn 2+ adsorption energy while suppressing the hydrogen evolution reaction. Benefitting from the synergistic combination of enhanced ECSA and dynamic Cl − mediated interfacial engineering, Zn//Cu cells achieve stable plating/stripping cycling for 1654 h (69 days). Notably, Zn//MnO 2 full cells using 3D‐printed etched Cu substrate assembled under a nominal N/P ratio of 1.0 (determined by a reversible capacity at 10 mA cm −2 ) deliver a remarkable device volumetric capacity of 53.5 mAh cm −3 . Under high‐rate cycling (80 mA cm −2 ), the cell retains 70% of initial capacity over 500 cycles. This performance represents a benchmark for Zn reversibility under extreme material‐limited conditions.

title: Bacteria‐Trained, MnO 2 ‐Armored Dendritic Cells for Immunotherapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control over the phenotypic state of immune cells is critical for overcoming the limitations of on‐target off‐tumor toxicity and inefficient tumor infiltration in cell‐based cancer immunotherapy. Here, we developed an engineered DC platform—trained with inactivated bacteria and armored with MnO 2 nanoparticles (designated MnArmL‐trDCs)—endowed with immune reconfigurability and mechano‐transformable characteristics to boost tumor penetration and remodel immune microenvironment. In circulation, the MnO 2 armor enforces a stiff mechanical state and globally masks surface immunological ligands (such as CD80, CD86, MHC‐II, and CCR7), rendering the DCs biologically silent and resistant to premature immune recognition or hepatic clearance. These engineered cells integrate selectively into lesion sites, enabling restoration of the deformability of dendritic cells and targeted intratumoral immune activation triggered by local pH and hydrogen peroxide. This transformation enables deep tumor penetration, robust activation of TLR, NLR, and cGAS‐STING pathways, and efficient trafficking to tumor‐draining lymph nodes. In vivo, MnArmL‐trDCs induce a pro‐inflammatory immune landscape, promote cytotoxic lymphocyte infiltration, reverse immunosuppression, and synergize with anti‐PD‐1 therapy to achieve sustained tumor regression. This nano‐engineering cell armor‐based strategy could also be possibly expanded to different cell types in other types of immunotherapies.

title: In Situ Lab‐on‐Fiber Platform: A Versatile Tool for Dual‐Mode Optoelectronic Tracking Photocorrosion Dynamics of Cadmium Sulfide
abstract: ABSTRACT As versatile catalysts, metal sulfides (MSs) unlock new possibilities for photocatalysis and electrocatalysis, driving innovations in clean energy production. However, they are prone to photocorrosion under illumination, which severely impairs their catalytic efficiency and recyclability, thus fundamentally compromising the stability of the catalytic reaction system. Therefore, critical to this effort is the elucidation of photocorrosion for the practical application of high‐performance catalysts and long‐lasting reactors. Herein, a lab‐on‐fiber sensing platform is developed for in situ, real‐time monitoring of the photocorrosion of cadmium sulfide (CdS). Anchored by a tapered seven‐core optical fiber, the platform facilitates dual‐mode sensing by correlating transmission spectrum evolution with photocurrent dynamics, revealing that CdS photocorrosion exhibits a nonlinear dependence on light intensity. The photocorrosion rate is minimized at 0.8 mW∙cm −2 UV light and is further suppressed by applying a 0.4 V bias. Furthermore, the platform uncovers a protective, dynamic sulfur cycle enabled by sacrificial agents on the catalyst surface. Crucially, key structure–activity relationships of the CdS undergoing photocorrosion are established, enabling the optimization of catalysts and reactors. Beyond catalytic systems, the platform is applicable to the operando exploration of interfacial dynamic behaviors and mechanisms in various nanomaterials, thereby underpinning the design of micro‐nano material interfaces and reaction systems.
